We will look after [the building and its contents], but we recognise that they will have to evolve if they are going to continue to meet diners’ needs.”Diners, however, can expect little change to the menu, she said – and crucially, no scones. “It’s not a National Trust menu, this is a very successful business in its own right. There will be no scones. That’s not their business.” Nor will there be preferential access or prices for National Trust members, “because it is a business, and it has to be successful,” she added. Instead, the charity is exploring options for virtual visits and other ways people could “feel like they are visiting the space” from afar.It was several years ago when Mayhew first approached the National Trust about a possible gift. Porten said while “excited by the offer”, they looked carefully at whether it was the right organisation to take on the building.View image in fullscreenThe storied restaurant has outlasted nine British monarchs and 45 prime ministers.Photograph: Jill Mead/The GuardianPorten said: “The nature of the National Trust, and the fact we have this extraordinary ability to take on places inalienably, for ever, means that we have to think about what’s right for now, but also to think about looking after them for future generations. That’s quite a big thing … It had to be quite a balanced response and decision.”Part of its value to the trust, she said, lay in helping the charity “tell different histories which are hard for us to tell at our other properties”.“You get a sense of all the delicious food which has been enjoyed here, the fine wines that have been consumed, the good company that’s been enjoyed. There’s something in the air about the conversations and the celebrations, the flirtations, the deals that have been struck, the heartbreak. All that hangs in the air, in a very magical way, [as] the backdrop to lots of different historical moments and lives.“It’s an extraordinary slice of the social history of London, and to have been here for so long - in this site and doing this business – is a very rare and special thing.”Explore more on these topicsRestaurantsThe National TrustFoodHeritageLondonnewsShareReuse this content

title: ‘There was a chance to stop him’: Parents react with fury to paedophile nursery worker revelations | Child protection | The Guardian
description: More than 50 families call for investigation into how Vincent Chan was allowed to return to job after inquiry by nursery
Author: Sirin Kale
Headline: More than 50 families call for investigation into how Vincent Chan was allowed to return to job after inquiry by nursery
Content: Vincent Chan was reported to his employer by a concerned parent in 2021 but was cleared to return to work.Photograph: Metropolitan Police/PAView image in fullscreenVincent Chan was reported to his employer by a concerned parent in 2021 but was cleared to return to work.Photograph: Metropolitan Police/PAChild protection‘There was a chance to stop him’: Parents react with fury to paedophile nursery worker revelationsMore than 50 families call for investigation into how Vincent Chan was allowed to return to job after inquiry by nurserySirin KaleInvestigations correspondentTue 13 Oct 2026 14.41 EDTLast modified on Tue 13 Oct 2026 15.11 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThe parents of the victims of paedophile nursery worker Vincent Chan have reacted with fury to the news that he was cleared to return to work after “significant concerns” wereraised by the parent of a young girl.As first revealedin the Guardian, Chan was reported to his employer, the nursery chain Bright Horizons, by a concerned parent in 2021.After being investigated by Bright Horizons, with the knowledge of Camden council, Chan was cleared to return to work at the nursery on the Finchley Road in north-westLondon. A year later, in 2022, Chan filmed himself abusing three-year-old girls in his care.“I feel a level of anger that I can barely put into words,” said one mother. Images of her daughter were found on Chan’s personal devices after his arrest.She added: “In 2021, around the time serious concerns had been raised about Vincent Chan, he was made my daughter’s key worker. We trusted him with her most intimate care, believing she was safe.“Knowing there was a chance to stop him before he had such extensive access to her is unbearable. I am heartbroken, but above all furious at Bright Horizons for failing to protect our children.”The families have called for an immediate “independent examination” of how the 2021 complaint was handled.In a statement issued by the law firm Leigh Day, which is representing 50 families affected by Chan’s abuse, they called for a “full and independent account of what happened, who knew what, when they knew it and why these decisions were made”.The parents of Chan’s victims have been promised answers in the form of a repeatedly delayed safeguarding review, led by an independent reviewer appointed by Camden council. But many expressed fury that they only learned the review had been pushed back to 2027 in the Guardian article.“Expressions of regret are meaningless,” said the parents in a statement. “Families deserve the truth about what happened, accountability for the decisions that were made, and action to make sure this cannot happen again. We cannot wait until 2027 for answers.”Get in touchContact our investigations teamThe best public interest journalism relies on first-hand accounts from people in the know. If you have something to share on this subject, you can contact us confidentially using the following methods:Secure Messaging in the Guardian appThe Guardian app has a tool to send tips about stories. Messages are end to end encrypted and concealed within the routine activity that every Guardian mobile app performs. This prevents an observer from knowing that you are communicating with us at all, let alone what is being said.If you don’t already have the Guardian app, download it (iOS/Android) and go to the menu. Select ‘Secure Messaging’.EmailIf you don’t need a high level of security or confidentiality you can emailinvestigations.contact@theguardian.com.SecureDropIf you can safely use the tor network without being observed or monitored you can send messages and documents to the Guardian via ourSecureDrop platform.Finally, our guide attheguardian.com/tipslists several ways to contact us securely, and discusses the pros and cons of each.Show moreThe families also restated their calls for Camden council to consider prosecuting Bright Horizons under health and safety legislation. “The Guardian’s report also strengthens the case for a criminal investigation,” they said.The row over the decision to clear Chan to return to work has overshadowed the Labour MP Sagal Abdi-Wali’s first week as an MP after her byelection victory in Holborn and St Pancras last week. Before becoming an MP, Abdi-Wali was leader of Camden council, presiding over the delayed review.Earlier on Tuesday Tulip Siddiq, the Labour MP for Hampstead and Kilburn, wrote to Camden council, asking it to commit to publishing the documentation relating to the 2021 investigation.“These revelations are causing significant distress to parents in my constituency, particularly the families directly affected by Chan’s crimes,” Siddiq wrote.“Families should not have to wait any longer for these answers,” she added.Camden council said: “We know the parents of the children who attended the nursery, and the wider public, will be concerned that a complaint was made about Vincent Chan to Bright Horizons in 2021 – and will want to know how this was responded to.“In 2021, Camden council’s local authority designated officer (LADO) provided advice to Bright Horizons, after Bright Horizons informed them (the LADO) of a complaint.“We have shared all relevant documents and information with the independent review team. We want families to get the answers they deserve, in full, through the outcome of the independent review.”A Bright Horizons spokesperson said: “We remain appalled by Vincent Chan’s crimes, and our thoughts are first and foremost with the children and families affected.“We strongly encourage parents to share all their concerns with the child safeguarding practice review (CSPR), which is being led by an independent reviewer and will rightly examine this case in full.“As the review is ongoing, we are unable to comment without the express written authorisation of the committee.”Explore more on these topicsChild protectionChildrenLondonCrimeChildcareLocal governmentEarly years educationnewsShareReuse this content

title: Man who died in Six Flags rollercoaster fall in Georgia was a father and educator | Georgia | The Guardian
description: Hassan Jihad Ibn Kariem was a father of 10-year-old daughter, and overcame two bouts of cancer, his family says
Author: Keely Aouga
Headline: Hassan Jihad Ibn Kariem was a father of 10-year-old daughter, and overcame two bouts of cancer, his family says
Content: The ‘Goliath’ rollercoaster at Six Flags Over Georgia.Photograph: Christopher Oquendo/ZUMA Press Wire/ShutterstockView image in fullscreenThe ‘Goliath’ rollercoaster at Six Flags Over Georgia.Photograph: Christopher Oquendo/ZUMA Press Wire/ShutterstockGeorgiaMan who died in Six Flags rollercoaster fall in Georgia was a father and educatorHassan Jihad Ibn Kariem was a father of 10-year-old daughter, and overcame two bouts of cancer, his family saysKeely AougaTue 13 Oct 2026 18.46 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GooglePolice on Tuesday identified the victim of thefatal accident at Six Flags Over Georgiaas 42-year-old Hassan Jihad Ibn Kariem of Atlanta.Kariem fell to his death after being ejected from his seat and several others were injured in an incident involving a rollercoaster at the theme park.Although authorities and Six Flags did not identify the rollercoaster, video footage shows passengers being evacuated from the park’s Goliath coaster.Kariem was a father to a 10-year-old daughter and an educator inAtlanta, Georgia.According to Atlanta public schools, Kariem started his career at Wesley International Academy as a technology teacher before being promoted to an IT Manager.“Atlanta Public Schools extends its deepest condolences to the family, friends, and loved ones of Mr Kariem,” a spokesperson for APS shared in a statement obtained by the Guardian.“He was a cherished member of the Wesley International Academy and APS families whose presence and impact will be deeply missed by our students, staff, and all those whose lives he touched,” the statement added.Wesley International Academy did not immediately return the Guardian’s request for comment.Kariem’s family spoke with11Alive’s Chase Houle, and shared that he overcame many challenges in life, including two bouts of cancer. The last stint was in 2018.Additionally, his family said Kariem and his daughter survived a car fire three weeks ago. The two were unharmed in the incident.Cobb county police department’s major crimes unit has launched an investigation into Kariem’s death.It was unknown what led to the fatal accident, nor how the others were injured or their conditions.Since Kariem’s death, Six Flagstemporarily closed nine rollercoastersacross six amusement parks around the US.The incident comes less than two weeks after Six Flags Magic Mountain in southern California announced thepermanent closure of its famous X2 rollercoasteramid lawsuits alleging serious brain injuries caused by the ride.The park had settled one wrongful death lawsuit from the family of a 22-year-old man who died after riding the coaster in 2022.Last year, a 32-year-old man died after riding a high-speed rollercoaster at the Universal Epic Universe theme park in Florida. He died from blunt impact injuries and his death was ruled accidental.According to a local Atlanta news station, Six Flags Over Georgia remains closed because of the offseason schedule and wasexpected to reopen on Friday.Explore more on these topicsGeorgiaTheme parksAtlantanewsShareReuse this content

title: Florida officials say six people dead from Hurricane Isaias | US weather | The Guardian
description: Governor Ron DeSantis says death toll ‘sad’ but praises work of local officials for helping to minimize storm’s impact
Author: Keely Aouga
Headline: Governor Ron DeSantis says death toll ‘sad’ but praises work of local officials for helping to minimize storm’s impact
Content: Damaged buildings in Pensacola Beach, Florida, after Hurricane Isaias made landfall.Photograph: Jen Golbeck/SOPA Images/ShutterstockView image in fullscreenDamaged buildings in Pensacola Beach, Florida, after Hurricane Isaias made landfall.Photograph: Jen Golbeck/SOPA Images/ShutterstockUS weatherFlorida officials say six people dead from Hurricane IsaiasGovernor Ron DeSantis says death toll ‘sad’ but praises work of local officials for helping to minimize storm’s impactKeely AougaTue 13 Oct 2026 17.25 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleSix deaths have been confirmed in Florida in the aftermath of Hurricane Isaias.In a press conference on Tuesday, Florida governor Ron DeSantis praised the work of local officials for minimizing the impact of the storm, whichmade landfalllate on Friday, ⁠bringing strong winds, rain, flash floods and tornado ​threats across parts of the ​US south-east, leaving hundreds of thousands ​of residents without power.DeSantis confirmed that there are six deaths linked to Hurricane Isaias, includingtwo previously confirmed deaths.One person was killed after a fallen tree on a home resulted in a direct fatality. Another individual was found deceased in their garage with a running generator in Escambia county.DeSantis confirmed that the remaining deaths linked to the storm include a car accident at an intersection, and storm-related disruptions to two people’s medical treatment.Despite there being half a dozen of deaths, the governor praised Floridians and local officials for taking proper precautions, linking it to there being a lower death toll, compared to previous storms.“We’re sad to hear that. At the same time, we’ve had some where there have been a lot more. So I think that people did take precautions and I think the local officials did a good job of spreading the word,” DeSantis said Tuesday.There are about 5,000 people in Florida state that remain without power north-west of where the storm landed, according to DeSantis.Free supplies are being provided at different locations of distribution to Floridians that have been impacted by the hurricane.Isaias is the first Atlantic hurricane of the 2026 season. As a result ofthe strong El Niño, it has been a notably quiet Atlantic hurricane season. The first hurricane of the season has not formed this late since 8 October 1905, which pre-dates the satellite era (1960s) for tracking hurricanes that has allowed for more non-landfall hurricanes to be discovered.Isaias is also the first hurricane tomake landfallin the continental US in two years, sinceMiltonstruck western Florida in October 2024.The National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (Noaa) said there is increasing likelihood of life-threatening storm surges along portions of the northern Gulf coast and damaging hurricane-force winds over portions of the Florida panhandle, southern Alabama andMississippi.Explore more on these topicsUS weatherHurricanesnewsShareReuse this content

title: Duane ‘Keffe D’ Davis sentenced to 40 years to life over Tupac Shakur’s murder | Tupac Shakur | The Guardian
description: ‘You don’t get to take a man from his family … and just walk away from it,’ judge says as former gang leader sentenced
Author: Uwa Ede-Osifo
Headline: ‘You don’t get to take a man from his family … and just walk away from it,’ judge says as former gang leader sentenced
Content: Duane ‘Keffe D’ Davis appears in court during his murder trial in Clark county district court in Las Vegas, Nevada, on 20 August.Photograph: Steve Marcus/ReutersView image in fullscreenDuane ‘Keffe D’ Davis appears in court during his murder trial in Clark county district court in Las Vegas, Nevada, on 20 August.Photograph: Steve Marcus/ReutersTupac ShakurDuane ‘Keffe D’ Davis sentenced to 40 years to life over Tupac Shakur’s murder‘You don’t get to take a man from his family … and just walk away from it,’ judge says as former gang leader sentencedTupac trial spotlights decades of US police failures in solving the caseUwa Ede-OsifoTue 13 Oct 2026 15.43 EDTFirst published on Tue 13 Oct 2026 15.03 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleDuane “Keffe D” Davis, the former California gang leaderconvictedof murder for orchestrating the 1996 fatal shooting of rapperTupac Shakur, has been sentenced to 40 years to life in prison.“For three years, I’ve heard you say some variation of the same thing … ‘Yeah, I was involved in this. But I’m different. I’ve moved on. I got out of Compton. I’m a grandfather now,’” Judge Carli Kierny said Tuesday as she delivered the sentence.“You don’t get to take a man from his family. You don’t get to take his very life, his whole future from him and just walk away from it,” Kierny continued.On 7 September 1996, Shakur was gunned down near theLas Vegasstrip shortly after a Mike Tyson boxing match. He succumbed to his injuries days later.For decades, hismurder remained unsolvedand one of hip-hop’s most enduring mysteries. Davis is the only person to beconvicted in connection to Shakur’s murder.“It was hard sitting, listening over and over and over again to someone describe – bit by bit, how they hunted Tupac Amaru Shakur down,” the rapper’s sister, Sekyiwa Shakur, said on Tuesday minutes before Davis was sentenced.She described her brother as a father figure. “He was who God trusted to take care of me,” she told the court.The grief from her brother’s murder led Sekyiwa Shakur to be hospitalized several times for depression, suicidal ideation and PTSD, she said.She and the rapper’s stepbrother, Maurice Shakur, called for Davis to face the maximum penalty.“Time to sit down and contemplate what you’ve done to the world, not just to me,” Sekyiwa Shakur said.Davis stared intently, but appeared stoic as the relatives spoke. He vowed earlier during the hearing to appeal the case.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Around 2-3 times a daySign up toBreaking News USGet the most important news as it breaksEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotion‘It always comes around’: fans react to conviction in Tupac Shakur’s murder 30 years laterRead moreA confluence of several factors hindered the investigation. The code of silence within street culture made some witnesses averse to police cooperation. Las Vegas police were skeptical about leads from their Compton counterparts, given that the head of security for Shakur’s record label was a former Compton cop.Orlando Anderson, a gangster and Davis’s nephew, was on law enforcement’s radar as the possible gunman. The night Shakur was killed, the young rap star got into an altercation with Anderson. Las Vegas police interviewed Anderson, but he was never arrested. Anderson later died in 1998.But then, in 2023, Davis wasarrestedon a murder charge.It was Davis’s own media tour, touting his status as one of the last surviving eyewitnesses, and a 2019 “tell-all” memoir that led to the breakthrough.Davis had felt emboldened by a 2008 backdoor deal he brokered with police. He spoke candidly to investigators about Shakur’s shooting, who had actually been seeking information about the death of Christopher Wallace, known as Biggie Smalls or The Notorious BIG. Under a proffer agreement, Davis was not to face charges for any offenses he shared.In his memoir, Compton Street Legend, Davis wrote that he and a group of other men targeted Shakur and his entourage, seeking retribution for the scuffle with his nephew.The memoir and the interview became central to prosecutors’ case. They argued the details amounted to a confession and that his public remarks voided the proffer agreement.During Davis’s murder trial, his defense team maintained that these details were embellished. They also argued, during the trial, that there was no physical evidence, such as a murder weapon, tying Davis to the Las Vegas slaying.Ultimately, jurors sided with the state.Explore more on these topicsTupac ShakurUS crimeWest CoastCaliforniaNevadaLas VegasnewsShareReuse this content

title: Enter the Zachbot: Trump’s new press secretary malfunctions on podium debut | Donald Trump | The Guardian
description: Katie Zacharia’s maiden briefing was excruciating – at least her predecessor had delivered her propaganda hot
Author: David Smith
Headline: Katie Zacharia’s maiden briefing was excruciating – at least her predecessor had delivered her propaganda hot
Content: Katie Zacharia, the new White House press secretary.Photograph: Ron Sachs-CNP/ShutterstockView image in fullscreenKatie Zacharia, the new White House press secretary.Photograph: Ron Sachs-CNP/ShutterstockThe US politics sketchDonald TrumpEnter the Zachbot: Trump’s new press secretary malfunctions on podium debutKatie Zacharia’s maiden briefing was excruciating – at least her predecessor had delivered her propaganda hotDavid Smithin WashingtonTue 13 Oct 2026 15.22 EDTLast modified on Tue 13 Oct 2026 19.55 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleWell, that was weird.Katie Zacharia, the new White House press secretary, made her debut on the podium on Tuesday with all the warmth, wisdom and political dexterityof an AI avatar.Zacharia was all stilted delivery, nervous tics and lack of eye contact. With an eerie lack of emotion, she served up pro-Trump talking points, took only three questions and vanished after 14 minutes. It was like the West Wing had turned intouncanny valley.The Zachbot’s past is indeed a bit of a mystery. The 41-year-old claims to be a lawyer but later a reporter asked when she passed the bar exam and shegave the unconvincing answer: “When I moved to China.” She was plucked from relative obscurity for the White House job after a brief gig at the Department of Homeland Security and a stint at the Trump Media and Technology Group.Wearing a dark jacket with big gold buttons on Tuesday morning, she entered the standing-room-only briefing room and stepped on to the podium as Trump’s sixth press secretary. For James Bond fans, that means we’ve reached the Daniel Craig era. For Doctor Who fans, it means the regeneration that brought usColin Baker(not the show’s golden age).Zacharia has the blond hair, glossy makeup and Fox News aesthetic of her immediate predecessorsKayleigh McEnanyandKaroline Leavitt(her name also begins with a “K” – surely a tell to the AI detectors). But it was Trump’s first press secretary, Sean Spicer, to whom she inadvertently paid homage.“Attendance is at record highs as enthusiastic, hard-working Americans are lining up and packing arenas to support President Trump and Republicans,” she said of Trump’s campaign rallies, echoing Spicer’s debut that falsely boasted of the biggest inaugural crowd ever.In truth, there have been plenty of empty seats at Trump’s rallies this time around and an unusually high number of interruptions from protesters.The Zachbot read from prepared notes about Trump’s many great accomplishments, awkwardly glancing up at her audience less than she should, smiling at odd moments and putting the emphasis on all the wrong words. “A great relationship …” (looks down, sighs, sounds like her cat just died) “with Venezuela”.It was bad. Toe-curlingly, don’t-know-where-to-look bad. At least Leavitt had delivered her propaganda hot. Evidently Trump’s communications team have found new and ingenious ways to torture reporters.Then came questions, first from rightwing Breitbart News, then rightwing Fox News, whose correspondentPeter Doocywondered whether the US had stopped sharing intelligence with Ukraine. The Zachbot froze for a millisecond. “I will have to get back to you on that,” came the auto response.Next up was the rightwing Daily Mail, asking aboutan alleged bribery scandalinvolving Kimberly Guilfoyle, the US ambassador to Greece, ex-fiancee of Donald Trump Jr and notorious screamer of “The best is yet to come!” The Zachbotsaid coldly: “We have asked Ambassador Guilfoyle to resign. She has been a wonderful asset to the team and we wish her well.”She nodded awkwardly. It was like every dystopian sci-fi film where the machine informs some hapless human that they will be terminated in 10 seconds.The Mail followed up with “a personal question” that would surely never be asked of a male press secretary: “Your family is in California. Your husband, your four children. I’m wondering how you are going to manage that.”The Zachbot gave her husband a shout-out and said she loved being with her children. “The idea of not spending evenings with my kids is completely unacceptable. So my president – excuse me, my husband – that’s a good one.”3:02Katie Zacharia holds awkward debut briefing as Trump's press secretary - videoA slip of the tongue! A glitch! Had someone spilled coffee on a cool, pitiless datacenter somewhere out in the California desert?The Zachbotwent on: “President Trump is the most family-friendly president we have ever had. He has hired more women with families and the fact that he knew I had four kids and he knew this job would be demanding and still placed his trust in me shows I know I’m capable of being able to step up to that.”Then she stunned everyone by wrapping it up and pledging that Trump would soon answer questions on the South Lawn. It was a tacit admission that the press secretary job is pointless when there is a president who talks all the time. But ironically, although the Zachbot took far fewer questions than others on their debut, she made more news with her Guilfoyle announcement.How long can she last? Trumpsaid soon after: “I thought she was very good.” But the Lincoln Project, an anti-Trump group,tweetedan image of the Zachbot beside a lettuce to evoke Liz Truss, who lasted only 49 days as British prime minister.And Anthony Scaramucci, who was Trump’s communications director for just 11 days, a period now known as “a Scaramucci”,tweeted: “The clock is running. Thus far 1/11th of a Scaramucci.”When the Mooch is giving you the Grim Reaper treatment, it might be time to self-terminate.Explore more on these topicsDonald TrumpThe US politics sketchUS politicsnewsShareReuse this content

title: Threat of AI share crash puts world financial stability at risk, says IMF | Economics | The Guardian
description: High valuations and debt put sector in danger, while fund also warns on government borrowing and cyber-attacks
Author: Heather Stewart
Headline: High valuations and debt put sector in danger, while fund also warns on government borrowing and cyber-attacks
Content: The IMF underlined the interconnected nature of big AI companies, and the high levels of borrowing being undertaken to fund investment in the sector.Photograph: Aly Song/ReutersView image in fullscreenThe IMF underlined the interconnected nature of big AI companies, and the high levels of borrowing being undertaken to fund investment in the sector.Photograph: Aly Song/ReutersEconomicsThreat of AI share crash puts world financial stability at risk, says IMFHigh valuations and debt put sector in danger, while fund also warns on government borrowing and cyber-attacksIMF warns global economy ‘could soon test the limits of resilience’Heather Stewartin Bangkok andKalyeena Makortoffin LondonTue 13 Oct 2026 08.30 EDTFirst published on Mon 12 Oct 2026 23.15 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThe threat of an AI share price crash rippling out across global markets is putting world financial stability at risk, the International Monetary fund has warned.In its twice-yearly Global Financial Stability Report, the IMF highlighted the sky-high valuations for AI companies along with their increasing debt pile as one reason that risks in the system are “elevated”.“The consequences of an AI correction could be global,” it warned. Aside from the US, Asian markets would be most exposed, and the UK and euro area potentially more insulated – though investors with US holdings would be hit.Athanasios Vamvakidis, the deputy director of the IMF’s monetary and capital department, launching the report, said: “The exposure of the rest of the world to US assets, particularly AI, is the highest it has ever been. So this is supporting the global economy through wealth effects today; but if we get a market correction it could have broad implications.”An AI crash was one of three “salient risks” to stability identified by the IMF, alongsiderising government borrowing costsand the threat of a big cyber-attack.It called this trio of factors “plausible near-term catalysts for a sharp tightening of financial conditions and market turmoil”.The IMF’s analysis underlined the interconnected nature of big AI companies, and the high levels of borrowing being undertaken to fund investment in the sector.“Weaker or less durable investment and profitability in AI could trigger a correction in AI-related asset prices, exacerbated by rising leverage, concentrated exposures, and circular financing arrangements,” it said.Such a reassessment would then “sharply reduce investment, trigger equity market corrections, and tighten financial conditions, with global spillovers”.The “magnificent seven” big tech stocks – Alphabet, Amazon, Apple, Meta, Microsoft, Nvidia and Tesla – account for more than 35% of the S&P 500 share index in the US, up from 12% a decade ago, and their total market capitalisation has increased by more than 50% in the past two years.Yet the IMF warned of “growing evidence” that the successful rollout of AI “may not require investment on the massive scale being undertaken by ‘hyperscaler’ firms”, and “potential economic gains may not be as large as expected”.The hyperscalers are the companies building the underlying infrastructure for the AI rollout, including many vast datacentres. They include Amazon Web Services, Google, Meta and Oracle.Shares in semiconductor companiesfell on Tuesdayafter the boss of Broadcom compared many AI investors to “casino” gamblers. Reports that the Chinese memory chip maker CXMT was making good progress on a new chip architecture also hit South Korean tech companies.The IMF also highlighted the growing leverage, or borrowing, that underpins the current boom and could amplify the effects of a crash.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toBusiness TodayGet set for the working day – we'll point you to all the business news and analysis you need every morningEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionIn particular, it identified soaring debts contracted by the companies themselves; hedge fund investment in the sector; and retail investors borrowing to speculate in AI stocks.In the event of an AI-led market downturn “these growing sources of leverage heighten the potential for forced selling and surges in equity volatility”, it said.It also pointed to the prevalence of“circular financing” deals, tying stronger AI companies to weaker partners in the same sector, and potentially exacerbating the impact of a share price correction.It identified $300bn (£227bn) worth of transactions between hyperscalers and “weaker AI firms” in just the past three years, supplemented by $650bn in debt, in exchange for $1.4tn in future financial commitments.In London, the chief executive of the UK’s Financial Conduct Authority, Nikhil Rathi, urged every small business across the financial sector to take out insurance to protect themselves against AI-related cybersecurity threats.He told MPs on the Commons Treasury committee that not all companies would have the resources to pay for access to “frontier” AI models such as Anthropic’s Mythos, which has been released on a restricted basis after it was said to be rapidly identifying gaps in government and corporate cybersecurity systems.“One message I’d give to every small business: you should consider making sure you are insured,” Rathi said.Explore more on these topicsEconomicsStock marketsTechnology sectorInternational Monetary Fund (IMF)AI (artificial intelligence)newsShareReuse this content

title: BBC asks judge to force Trump to sit for deposition as part of his $10bn lawsuit | BBC | The Guardian
description: BBC asks US federal judge to compel Trump’s lawyers to schedule deposition after his team canceled initial session
Author: Jeremy Barr
Headline: BBC asks US federal judge to compel Trump’s lawyers to schedule deposition after his team canceled initial session
Content: Donald Trump sued the BBC for up to $10bn in damages over edited clips of a speech he gave during a rally on 6 January 2021.Photograph: Bloomberg/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenDonald Trump sued the BBC for up to $10bn in damages over edited clips of a speech he gave during a rally on 6 January 2021.Photograph: Bloomberg/Getty ImagesBBCBBC asks judge to force Trump to sit for deposition as part of his $10bn lawsuitBBC asks US federal judge to compel Trump’s lawyers to schedule deposition after his team canceled initial sessionJeremy Barrin WashingtonTue 13 Oct 2026 16.49 EDTLast modified on Tue 13 Oct 2026 18.22 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThe BBC is asking a federal judge inFloridato forceDonald Trumpto sit for a deposition as part of the president’s $10bn defamation lawsuit against the British broadcaster.According to a Tuesday filing, theBBCand Trump’s legal team had agreed for him to be deposed on Friday. The BBC’s lawyers wrote to the judge that they have spent months trying to secure a location for the deposition from Trump’s team.On 28 September, Trump’s lawyers told the BBC’s counsel that the president “is no longer available for his deposition on October 16 due to other matters of national importance”.While Trump’s lawyers said they would follow up quickly with a replacement date, they did not, ultimately suggesting that he would be available in the second or third week of January, well after the deadline to complete the discovery portion of the case. Lawyers for the BBC had pledged to keep the location of the deposition confidential.As such, the BBC’s lawyers are now asking the judge to require Trump’s team to schedule the deposition.“Plaintiff chose to file this lawsuit and, in doing so, he accepted the obligations of civil litigation,” the BBC’s motion reads. “The BBC therefore asks the Court to compel Plaintiff to confirm a date for his deposition, notify the BBC of a secure location where such deposition is possible and any other logistics required to ensure Plaintiff’s safety, and sit for the deposition, as the core rules of discovery require.”Magistrate judge Enjoliqué Aytch Lett has scheduled a discovery hearing that is likely to touch on the deposition issue for 22 October.“Nearly eight months into discovery, after seven depositions of BBC witnesses, and with only two months of discovery remaining, the BBC still has not been able to depose, and does not even have a schedule to depose, the most central figure in this case: Plaintiff himself,” lawyers for the BBC wrote in the Tuesday motion.Trump, who has a long history of legal action against media companies, filed a lawsuit against the BBC in December 2025, accusing the network of violating Florida’s Unfair and Deceptive Trade Practices Act over the edit of a Panorama documentary that edited together comments he made during a rally on 6 January 2021. The BBC has apologized for the error.“The formerly respected and now disgraced BBC defamed President Trump by intentionally, maliciously, and deceptively doctoring his speech in a brazen attempt to interfere in the 2024 Presidential Election,” a spokesperson for Trump’s legal team said in a statement. “The BBC has a long pattern of deceiving its audience in coverage of President Trump, all in service of its own leftist political agenda. President Trump’s powerhouse lawsuit is holding the BBC accountable for its defamation and reckless election interference just as he has held other fake news mainstream media responsible for their wrongdoing.”Explore more on these topicsBBCDonald TrumpLaw (US)newsShareReuse this content

title: ​FTC and seven states seek contempt ruling against Shkreli over pharma ban | Martin Shkreli | The Guardian
description: Martin Shkreli’s 2022 release conditions bar him from participating in the pharmaceutical industry, including ownership stakes or business decisions
Author: Maya Yang
Headline: Martin Shkreli’s 2022 release conditions bar him from participating in the pharmaceutical industry, including ownership stakes or business decisions
Content: Martin Shkreli speaking to the press in 2017 after the jury issued a verdict in his case at the US direct court for the eastern district in New York City.Photograph: Drew Angerer/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenMartin Shkreli speaking to the press in 2017 after the jury issued a verdict in his case at the US direct court for the eastern district in New York City.Photograph: Drew Angerer/Getty ImagesMartin Shkreli​FTC and seven states seek contempt ruling against Shkreli over pharma banMartin Shkreli’s 2022 release conditions bar him from participating in the pharmaceutical industry, including ownership stakes or business decisionsMaya YangTue 13 Oct 2026 12.54 EDTLast modified on Tue 13 Oct 2026 13.44 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThe Federal Trade Commission (FTC) and seven US states have alleged that pharmaceutical executive Martin Shkreli repeatedly violated alifetime banon participating in the pharmaceutical industry, and they are asking a judge to hold him in contempt.In amotionfiled on Tuesday in US district court in New York City, the FTC and its state co-plaintiffs allege that 43-year-old Shkreli – nicknamed the “Pharma Bro” – has traded stocks in at least 60 pharmaceutical companies and publicly commented on their businesses since his release from prison in May 2022.Conditions related to Shkreli’s release prohibit him from directly or indirectly participating in the pharmaceutical industry, including owning stakes in pharmaceutical companies or influencing their business decisions.Martin Shkreli ban from pharmaceutical industry upheld by US courtRead moreThe FTC alleges that Shkreli publicized his activities through live streams and posts on the YouTube, X and Reddit platforms. During one live stream, he told viewers: “I’m showing you how to trade and invest in biotech,” according to the FTC.In another live stream, Shkreli allegedly revealed what he described as his “magic trick”, saying: “It doesn’t matter what trades I make because I can always find a couple of biotech stocks to smoke.”The FTC also alleges Shkreli used his live streams to organize public campaigns to short pharmaceutical stocks based on predictions that companies’ clinical trials would fail.For those “brazen violations”, the FTC’s court filing said: “Shkreli should be held in civil contempt and face sanctions to purge his current contempt and to coerce his future compliance.”The court filing said that should include, but not be limited to, “a complete accounting of his pharmaceutical company stock trades, divestment of any ownership in any pharmaceutical company, a monetary fine in the amount of Shkreli’s profits made through his contumacious conduct, and clear and escalating consequences – including additional fines and incarceration – for any future violations”.Shkreli’s pharmaceutical industry ban stems from a2022 rulingthat found he had conducted an illegal anticompetitive scheme to raise the price of Daraprim – a drug used to treat malaria, certain cancers and toxoplasmosis – by more than 5,000%, from $17.50 to $750 per tablet.That same year, a US court fined Shkreli $64.6m, describing his conduct as “egregious, deliberate, repetitive, long-running and ultimately dangerous [and] illegal”.“Defendants must fulfill their obligations” when a court issues an order, the FTC competition bureau director, Daniel Guarnera, said on Tuesday. He added that Tuesday’s filing against Shkreli “should serve as notice that the FTC will not hesitate to enforce violations of court orders”.Similarly, the New York attorney general, Letitia James,saidof Shkreli: “A court-ordered lifetime ban isn’t a suggestion. Martin Shkreli has been livestreaming his pharmaceutical company trades for the world to see, in violation of the law.“Shkreli’s market manipulation and monopolistic tactics put investors and the public at risk, and we’re going back to court to put a stop to his latest illegal behavior.”The Guardian has approached Shkreli for comment.Shkreli in 2018 was sentenced to seven years in prison after being found guilty of two counts of securities fraud and one count of securities fraud conspiracy. He became a symbol of corporate greed before being released from prison early.Explore more on these topicsMartin ShkreliPharmaceuticals industryUS justice systemContempt of courtnewsShareReuse this content

title: Is punishing the poor Trump’s last hand to play? | Donald Trump | The Guardian
description: The pre-midterm defenestration of ACA enrollees looks like political madness – but the president appears to believe hitting poor people might work for him
Author: Eduardo Porter
Headline: The pre-midterm defenestration of ACA enrollees looks like political madness – but the president appears to believe hitting poor people might work for him
Content: Donald Trump at a rally in San Antonio, Texas, last week.Photograph: Mandel Ngan/AFP/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenDonald Trump at a rally in San Antonio, Texas, last week.Photograph: Mandel Ngan/AFP/Getty ImagesDonald TrumpAnalysisIs punishing the poor Trump’s last hand to play?Eduardo PorterThe pre-midterm defenestration of ACA enrollees looks like political madness – but the president appears to believe hitting poor people might work for himSend us your questions on how the US economy is shaping the midterm electionsTue 13 Oct 2026 07.00 EDTLast modified on Tue 13 Oct 2026 16.20 EDTShareThere is a manic quality toDonald Trump’s desperate dash to do something, anything, ahead of November’smidterm electionsto convince beleaguered Americans that he can make the pressures his policies have imposed on their livelihoods go away.The US presidentofferedto lower barriers against beef imports to limit surging meat prices, only to considerbacktrackingunderpressurefrom the cow lobby. Heofferedto stop diesel exports, only to find oil companieswerenot interested. He weakened fuel efficiency standards, claiming this would trim the price of a new car (and forgetting to point out it will also raise spending on gas). In early October he started mailing$500 checksto nearly a million people touting his healthcare “wins”. Oh, and he promised adult Americans a$5,000 checkif Republicans maintain control of Congress. That, too, willgo nowhere.In the face of such setbacks, maybe Trump felt he had to demonstrate he still can get something done. Still, it is somewhat counterintuitive that the administration, in the shape of Vice-President JD Vance, decided to broadcast the one initiative it did manage to bring to fruition:ejectingmore than 750,000 enrollees from the Affordable Care Act (ACA) health insurance marketplaces, on grounds that they are not entitled to federal subsidies.Trump immigrant purge could cut social security for Americans by $2,000 a yearRead moreTrump could argue that the cuts fit within the administration’s promised commitment to restore fiscal discipline. But that part of the platform – which came as Scott Bessent, the treasury secretary, promised to trim the budget deficit to 3% of US gross domestic product – was never more than a rhetorical feint.The pre-midterm defenestration of ACA enrollees by Trump’s “fraud taskforce”, by contrast, looks a lot like political madness, given the persistent economic anxieties articulated by Democratic and Republican voters across the country.The savings from the ACA maneuver, estimated by the administration at $2.2bn per year, are chump change compared with the centerpiece of Trump’s fiscal policy – the One Big Beautiful Bill Act from 2025 that is expected to add $4.1tn to budget deficits over the next decade, largely due to tax cuts benefiting the most affluent Americans.PaceBessent, the budget deficit is growing rapidly, expected to rise to some $2tn in the fiscal year of 2026, roughly 6% of GDP and about 18% more than in fiscal 2024, the last year of the Biden administration.Rather than stem budgetary red ink, it’s as if Trump’s objective is tospread miserybeyond the 3 million Americans who had to drop their health insurance after the administration last year cancelled subsidies offered by the Biden administration.View image in fullscreenKimberly Brandt of the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services holds up a poster depicting a headshot of Cory Lloyd, convicted of Affordable Care Act fraud, as Mehmet Oz speaks during a conference on 22 September in Washington DC.Photograph: Andrew Harnik/Getty ImagesThe effort is something out of the playbook of Elon Musk’sDoge. His promise to rid the government of “waste” and “fraud” probably caused the deaths ofmillions of childrenin the developing world after thedismantlingof USAID, butprovedlargelyirrelevanttothe task of saving money for the government. It may serve as a masterclass in trolling. But it is not a vote-winner.Part of Trump’s brain seems to understand this. Trump paid in part for the “beautiful” bill’s colossal tax cut bycuttingfunding to Medicaid and theSnapfoodstampprogramfor low-income Americans. But he engineered most of the cuts to kick in after the midterms to minimize the political cost. The thinking was that lower-income Americans would happily vote for the Republicans out of gratitude for their somewhat bigger tax refund checks this year and tax breaks for overtime and tips (cleverly designed to expire at the end of Trump’s term) and not notice the cuts rushing down the pike on federal programs they relied on.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toBusiness TodayGet set for the working day – we'll point you to all the business news and analysis you need every morningEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionBut the new evictions from the ACA suggest that his brain’s darker side is winning. Indeed, it underscores Trump’s belief that hitting poor people might work for him. Rather than a commitment to sound fiscal policy, a helping hand for American families treading water or an economic platform of any kind, Trump’s latest exercise in “fraud prevention” points to a strategy revolving around punishing people he can define as “bad”. Deep underwater in the polls for his nutty stewardship of the economy, among other things, Trump seems to believe that his one remaining winning card is to do violence against constituencies that his base may not like. Top of the list are immigrants and low-income people. And so it is that ICE is also doubling down,announcingit will hire another 5,000 agents by the end of the year.A national verdict on Trump 2.0 is coming. Nine midterm voters share where they standRead moreThe president is on to something. About two-thirds of Republicans believe giving more aid to the poor does more harm than good, according to surveysfrom the Pew Research Center. Despite the repeated instances of abuse by federal agents, only 19% of Republicans think the Trump administration isdoing too muchto deport immigrants illegally in the country. The mostradical rightwingvoters are all in for federal deportations and don’t think the federal government should be responsible for ensuring Americans’ healthcare.Perhaps Trump’s heart truly lies on the dark side. But doubling down on policies to please the most ardent fanatics in his base ultimately reveals the weakness of Trump’s position. Perhaps even he understands that he haslost the rest of the country. Punishing the poor and the foreign – alongside an unlikely $5,000 Hail Mary pass – is all he has left.Eduardo Porter is a journalist focused on economics and politics. He writes the newsletterBeing Thereon SubstackExplore more on these topicsDonald TrumpUS economyUS politicsEconomicsUS domestic policyTrump administrationUS healthcareanalysisShareReuse this content

title: ‘Chip on his shoulder’: Brian Flores lawyers condemn racial stereotypes in NFL coaching report | NFL | The Guardian
description: Unsealed recruiting report on Vikings coordinator contains alleged racial stereotypes and references his ongoing discrimination lawsuit against the NFL
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Unsealed recruiting report on Vikings coordinator contains alleged racial stereotypes and references his ongoing discrimination lawsuit against the NFL
Content: Vikings defensive coordinator Brian Flores’ lawyers have accused the NFL of racial discrimination and retaliation over a newly unsealed recruiting report.Photograph: Matt Krohn/APView image in fullscreenVikings defensive coordinator Brian Flores’ lawyers have accused the NFL of racial discrimination and retaliation over a newly unsealed recruiting report.Photograph: Matt Krohn/APNFL‘Chip on his shoulder’: Brian Flores lawyers condemn racial stereotypes in NFL coaching reportRecruiting report prepared for Raiders’ 2024 searchLawyers say assessment contains racial stereotypesFlores sued NFL over discriminatory hiring in 2022Associated PressTue 13 Oct 2026 19.39 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleA recently unsealed recruiting report on Brian Flores contains multiple examples of “racial stereotypes” and amounts to unlawful retaliation for the coach’s discrimination lawsuit against theNFL, according to his lawyers.The Korn Ferry report, made public on Tuesday and obtained by the Associated Press, lists six strengths and seven weaknesses that Flores’ attorneys say demonstrate the league’s continued reliance on racial stereotypes in hiring and its retaliation against the coach for his lawsuit alleging racial discrimination.The report, first published by Front Office Sports, was prepared in connection with the Las Vegas Raiders’ head coaching vacancy in 2024. Flores is now the defensive coordinator for theMinnesota Vikings.Former NFL star Mark Sanchez reaches settlement over stabbing altercationRead more“The recently unsealed documents demonstrate two unfortunate, but unsurprising, realities,” attorney Michael J Willemin said in a statement. “First, that Mr Flores’ decision to hold the league and its teams accountable for systemic race discrimination has been met with unlawful retaliation. Second, discrimination continues to play a significant role in the hiring process for NFL Head Coaches, as evidenced by the fact that the candidate profile prepared for the Raiders leans heavily on racial stereotypes.”Willemin added: “We and Mr Flores are committed to eradicating the institutional racism and retaliation that permeates the league, its teams and their partners.”The NFL did not immediately respond to a request for comment.One of the strengths listed in the report describes Flores as “polished and a good presenter despite growing up in Brownsville, Brooklyn (same as Mike Tyson). He was able to build a strong friendship with a billionaire’s son which gave him opportunities to socialize and learn how to build relationships with white-collar and upper-class individuals.”Brownsville is a predominantly Black and Hispanic neighborhood in Brooklyn.One of the weaknesses says Flores “can fool you with his polish upwards. Has little people skills, lacks self-awareness and can sometimes exhibit erratic behavior.”The report also cites comments by former Dolphins quarterback Tua Tagovailoa, saying they had contributed to a narrative that Flores was “pessimistic and adversarial” and that his coaching style had “shattered his confidence”.Other criticisms included claims that Flores’ “personality is unpredictable” and that he “once threatened violence to his GM and made irrational demands during an ownership meeting”.The report quotes an unnamed longtime senior executive who said Flores “may have changed since, but he was the worst hiring decision we’ve ever made”.The final weakness listed was that Flores’ ongoing discrimination lawsuit against the NFL could become a distraction.Flores, who is Black, sued the league and three teams in February 2022, alleging the NFL was “rife with racism” in its hiring practices involving Black coaches. He had recently been fired as head coach of theMiami Dolphins.Two other Black coaches, Steve Wilks and Ray Horton, subsequently joined the lawsuit.Explore more on these topicsNFLMinnesota VikingsMiami DolphinsUS sportsShareReuse this content

title: Former NFL star Mark Sanchez reaches settlement over stabbing altercation | NFL | The Guardian
description: Former NFL quarterback Mark Sanchez has reached an agreement in principle with the truck driver who stabbed him during an altercation
Author: Guardian sport
Headline: Former NFL quarterback Mark Sanchez has reached an agreement in principle with the truck driver who stabbed him during an altercation
Content: Mark Sanchez moved into broadcasting after his NFL career.Photograph: Brooke Sutton/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenMark Sanchez moved into broadcasting after his NFL career.Photograph: Brooke Sutton/Getty ImagesNFLFormer NFL star Mark Sanchez reaches settlement over stabbing altercationFormer QB fought with 69-year-old last OctoberFox Sports parted ways with Sanchez over incidentSanchez was charged over Indianapolis confrontationGuardian sportand agenciesTue 13 Oct 2026 16.27 EDTLast modified on Tue 13 Oct 2026 16.31 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleFormer NFL quarterback and Fox Sports analyst Mark Sanchez has reached an agreement in principle with the truck driverwho stabbed himduring an altercation last October,according to the Athletic.Sanchez was stabbed and pepper sprayed by Perry Tole, who was 69 at the time,during the incident in Indianapolis, where the former New York Jets star was due to cover an NFL game between the Colts and Las Vegas Raiders. Prosecutors said Tole used pepper spray and a knife to defend himself ​after Sanchez attempted to enter ‌his truck during an argument over a parking spot.Former NFL star Mark Sanchez ‘focused on recovery’ after jail appearance over stabbing incidentRead moreTole suffered “significant injuries to his head, jaw and neck” and ‌was seeking damages for his injuries, according to court documents in the civil case. The incident left Sanchez with stab wounds to his torso, and the former quarterback later said the surgeon who operated on him “saved my life”.Last month, Sanchez’s lawyers filed a motion to plead guilty to at least one charge in his criminal case; that charge has not been specified. He was charged with one felony count of battery resulting in serious ‌bodily injury, and misdemeanor charges of unauthorized entry of a motor vehicle, public intoxication endangering the life of another, and battery resulting ​in bodily injury. A hearing in Sanchez’s criminal case is scheduled for next month.Fox Sports cut ties with Sanchez after his arrest.Sanchez joined Fox in 2021 and also contributed to FS1 studio programming. Before his broadcasting career, Sanchez played 10 seasons in the NFL with several teams, including theJets, who took him with the fifth overall pick of the 2009 draft. He later played for the Philadelphia Eagles and Dallas Cowboys. He retired in July 2019 and soon after began working with ESPN’s college football coverage before moving to Fox.Explore more on these topicsNFLNew York JetsUS sportsUS sports medianewsShareReuse this content

title: Barrios strikes after 53 seconds as Atlético pile misery on 10-man Manchester United  | Champions League | The Guardian
description: Pablo Barrios struck after 53 seconds and Leny Yoro was shown red as Atlético Madrid added to Manchester United’s woes with a 2-0 victory
Author: Sid Lowe
Headline: Pablo Barrios struck after 53 seconds and Leny Yoro was shown red as Atlético Madrid added to Manchester United’s woes with a 2-0 victory
Content: Pablo Barrios (No 8) celebrates after firing Atlético Madrid ahead inside the first minute.Photograph: Juanjo Martin/EPAView image in fullscreenPablo Barrios (No 8) celebrates after firing Atlético Madrid ahead inside the first minute.Photograph: Juanjo Martin/EPAChampions LeagueBarrios strikes after 53 seconds as Atlético pile misery on 10-man Manchester UnitedSid Loweat the Riyadh Air MetropolitanoTue 13 Oct 2026 17.10 EDTLast modified on Tue 13 Oct 2026 19.10 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleMichael Carrick had seen it in his players, he said, but no one else can. Not so far in the Premier League, where they have sufferedtheir worst start in 40 years, and not here in Madrid, where Manchester United’s head coach insisted they would embrace the challenge. The reaction was coming, he promised; he had looked at them and was sure of it. Instead, they were a goal down after just 53 seconds and all that came was the old familiar sting, that early opener from Pablo Barrios and a second from Ademola Lookman condemning them to another defeat.So much for a reaction, a rebellion: in their place a kind of resignation, a sense that maybe this is just United’s reality: a game that began badly, did not get very much better, and finished even worse. True, the result could have been different, Bryan Mbeumo unable to convert two first-half chances while Bruno Fernandes struck the bar and put an opportunity wide, but that did not diminish the feeling that something is really wrong. It may even have deepened it.‘I expect more’: Lisandro Martínez hits out at Manchester United hierarchyRead moreEven the late, harsh red card for Leny Yoro which can be offered in mitigation did not change a simple fact: at the end of another insipid night, United lost. Unitedarelost, perhaps.“Sometimes when it’s not quite going for you, you see who’s really there,” United’s manager said the night before, a message that perhaps hinted at something rotten beneath the surface, but on the opening goal no one was really there. They weren’t there on the left, where Lee Kang-in’s pass sent Álex Baena into a wide-open space; they weren’t there to close him down as he cut into the area; and they weren’t there on the right either, where Barrios was running through alone. Baena laid across and Barrios’s shot went off Ayden Heaven and into the net.Barrios held up six fingers, the number of the club captain, Koke, whose mother had died in the hours before kick-off. From the bench Koke’s shirt was raised. All around the Metropolitano, supporters roared. This was set, it seemed.Although another effort from Baena soon hit Lisandro Martínez, United did find a foothold and could have found a way back. Mbeumo had two clear chances in quick succession: the first, after nice footwork on the right, went wide; the second, following a neat exchange with Youri Tielemans, was stopped by Jan Oblak on the other side. From the corner, Carlos Baleba headed straight at the keeper.View image in fullscreenBruno Fernandes reacts after Manchester United concede a second goal, scored by Ademola Lookman.Photograph: Adam Davy/PAThat was short-lived, though, Atlético soon asserting themselves, moving the ball with a pace and conviction United couldn’t match. Barrios and Baena couldn’t be controlled, and the spaces they opened were vast. The pressure United applied tended to arrive late or not at all. On the touchline too the contrast was stark: Diego Simeone prowled, Carrick stood motionless in the corner of his technical area, chin in his hand. The Argentinian was booked for waving an imaginary card. Maybe United’s manager could try that. Something, anyway.By half-time, Atlético had enjoyed 66% of possession. They could also have had a greater lead. Álex Grimaldo rattled a superb free‑kick off the bar and just before the break Johnny Cardoso’s sweeping finish was ruled out when the video assistant referee revealed a Marcos Llorente handball in the buildup. The second half then began with a neatly floated ball from Barrios setting up Julián Álvarez to volley against a post. Again, the space, time and the ease with which the move played out was just too big.At the other end, Bruno Fernandes then had a wonderful opportunity to level it. Tielemans did superbly to find him, the ball sitting up and Oblak coming off his line to meet him – the kind of opportunity, in short, that is supposed to end only one way but that this time ended another.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionUnited’s captain lifted the ball past the keeper and wide. Soon, Atlético were back again, Baena bending a shot wide, although Atlético appeared to have settled, the game drifting. That perhaps suited United: with Atlético’s threat no longer so present, the ball was theirs for the first time and the lead was still only one, opportunity there. Fernandes, increasingly involved, swung a shot against the bar.View image in fullscreenLeny Yoro trudges off after being shown a red card.Photograph: Adam Davy/PAWhich was when it finally, definitively and far too easily fell apart. Suddenly, on 74 minutes, Jonathan David was running through the middle on to a Morten Hjulmand ball. Yoro went with him, grappling as they ran, and the pair fell. Although Glenn Nyberg didn’t give a foul, allowing the move to play out with David scrambling the ball to Lookman, a voice in his ear called him to the screen to watch the challenge again. When he returned, he had a red in his hand.The decision felt harsh. It was also the end. Three minutes later, Atlético were running through United again. Grimaldo slotted a pass into David, inside the area and, although his shot was saved by Senne Lammens, Lookman was there to score. Heaven and Fernandes were removed; this was done, nothing left to fight for, not that they had fought much in the first place, the reaction postponed for some other day.Explore more on these topicsChampions LeagueAtlético MadridManchester Unitedmatch reportsShareReuse this content

title: Athletics wishes it could scrub the women’s marathon world record – what can be done? | Athletics | The Guardian
description: Ruth Chepngetich’s failed doping test, five months after she obliterated the record in 2024, left the sport deeply uneasy but powerless to act
Author: Sean Ingle
Headline: Ruth Chepngetich’s failed doping test, five months after she obliterated the record in 2024, left the sport deeply uneasy but powerless to act
Content: Ruth Chepngetich, who has since been banned for a doping violation, took nearly two minutes off the women’s marathon world record in Chicago in 2024.Photograph: Patrick Gorski/USA Today SportsView image in fullscreenRuth Chepngetich, who has since been banned for a doping violation, took nearly two minutes off the women’s marathon world record in Chicago in 2024.Photograph: Patrick Gorski/USA Today SportsAthleticsAthletics wishes it could scrub the women’s marathon world record – what can be done?Sean IngleRuth Chepngetich’s failed doping test, five months after she obliterated the record in 2024, left the sport deeply uneasy but powerless to actTue 13 Oct 2026 03.00 EDTShareWhen Ruth Chepngetich annihilated the women’s marathon world record in Chicago two years ago today,NBC’s commentators compared it to the moon landing. “Bring it on Neil Armstrong!” cried one. “She has done things in this sport that we have not seen,” said another. “Unbelievable!”That was a word others reached for too after the Kenyan had crossed the line in 2hr 9min 56sec, a time that not only smashed the world record by 1min 57sec, but her personal best by a staggering five minutes. Afterwards she wasasked by Robert Johnson of Let’s Runwhat her response was to those who believed she must be doping. “People must talk,” she replied. “I don’t know.”Marathon world record holder Ruth Chepngetich suspended over banned substanceRead moreWe know a lot more now. Because five months after that epic run, Chepngetich’s star came crashing down to earth. First she failed a doping test.Then she was banned for three years. These days people in the sport talk about her reluctantly, like a family member who has joined a mysterious cult. Yet her world record still stands because she passed a test after the race itself.What should we think of this? What are we allowed legally to say about this? And what, if anything, can be done about it?A couple of weeks ago, I spoke to Brett Clothier, the head of theAthleticsIntegrity Unit, which prosecuted the case against Chepngetich, to ask about her world record. “It is not satisfactory, to be frank,” he admitted. “But the world anti-doping code is pretty clearcut on the rights athletes have, even if they’re found guilty of a doping offence.”That much is true. But while legally Chepngetich was clean when she broke her world record, the fact it stands surely damages the sport’s credibility.True, there are plenty of highly suspicious records from the 80s and early 90s, given what we know about state-sponsored doping behind the iron curtain and in China. And if you believe Florence Griffith Joynerknocked more than half a secondoff her 100m and 200m times in 1988 by doing 5,000 sit-ups a day and drinking water, I have some magic beans to sell you.Griffith Joyner, of course, never tested positive. But before her death aged 38, her fellow American sprinter Darrell Robinson claimed in a paid interview with the German magazine Stern that he had sold her human growth hormone for $2,000.View image in fullscreenHer world record remains on the books, but Ruth Chepngetich is banned from competing until 2028.Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The GuardianHe also alleged that she had told him: “If you want to make a million dollars, you’ve got to invest a couple of thousand.” Yet as much as Flo-Jo’s records make us uneasy, they are seen as coming from a bygone and more lawless era.Also, what makes Chepngetich unique is that no other athlete has been hit with a lengthy ban so soon after a world record.The Kenyan’s defence for being 20 times the legal limit of hydrochlorothiazide (HCTZ) in her system? That she had taken her housemaid’s medication after feeling hot and having a rapid resting heartbeat.It was, the AIU noted, a “hardly credible” explanation.The AIU also found screenshots on Chepngetich’s phone about the banned drug testosterone and “messages related to unidentified third parties working on ‘programs’ possibly related to doping”. The Kenyan has insisted that she has never used testosterone and the messages were from a group chat, but they hardly inspire confidence either.So what can be done? The short answer, having spoken to the World Anti-Doping Agency (Wada), is very little. As a Wada spokesperson pointed out to me, removing her results before her positive test “in the absence of any evidence or reasonable inference that the athlete was doping before or at the time of the earlier results, might well breach a number of legal principles including proportionality and human rights.”skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toSport in FocusOur picture editors select their favourite sporting images from the past week, from the spectacular to the powerful, and with a little bit of fun thrown inEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionBut what about Lance Armstrong, who wasstripped of his Tour de France titlesdespite not being convicted of breaking any doping rules while competing? Could this not apply here? Not according to Wada.“He had procedural avenues open to him to contest the sanction but ultimately chose not to use them,” a spokesperson told me. “That makes his case a relatively weak precedent for establishing how far retrospective disqualification could legally go.”One idea I floated to various experts was the idea that athletes could be asked to sign a social contract, which pledged they would accept losing their world record if they tested positive within a year of that world record or winning an Olympic medal.In theory, one anti-doping expert put it to me, it was possible to do this. But he felt it would require everybody – from sports federations and governments to athlete bodies and human rights groups – to buy in and to agree to change the Wada code to allow retrospective punishments. And that is not going to happen.At least track and field can point to many significant victories over doping in the last decade, given that Chepngetich is one of 317 elite Kenyan athletes the AIU has caught since it was set up in 2017. Many sports pay lip service to catching cheats. Athletics actually does. And the AIU does it on a modest budget of $11.9m (£9m) a year.There are also positive signs that prominent athletesrealise more must be donewhen it comes to anti-doping. Before Sabastian Saweset his men’s marathon world recordin London, for instance, his sponsors, Adidas, paid $50,000 for extra testing. Nike did the same for two of their athletes, Jacob Kiplimo and Brigid Kosgei, before Chicago.Sawe’s agent, Eric Lilot, wants to go further by making his athletes sign a contract that will require them to give up any money still owed to them if it is shown they intentionally tried to dope. All that points to brighter days ahead, however much Chepngetich’s record makes us feel queasy.Explore more on these topicsAthleticsMarathonDrugs in sportcommentShareReuse this content

title: WNBA moves finals schedule to allow Atlanta Dream to play at larger arena | WNBA | The Guardian
description: The league has rescheduled two games against Golden State to accommodate the Dream at the 17,000-seat State Farm Arena, with a potential Game 6 venue still unresolved
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: The league has rescheduled two games against Golden State to accommodate the Dream at the 17,000-seat State Farm Arena, with a potential Game 6 venue still unresolved
Content: The Atlanta Dream have played six regular-season games and three home playoff games at State Farm Arena this season, and will make the 17,000-seat venue their permanent home in 2027.Photograph: Jonathan Bachman/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenThe Atlanta Dream have played six regular-season games and three home playoff games at State Farm Arena this season, and will make the 17,000-seat venue their permanent home in 2027.Photograph: Jonathan Bachman/Getty ImagesWNBAWNBA moves finals schedule to allow Atlanta Dream to play at larger arenaGame 3 moved up a day to avoid conflictDream to host at 17,000-seat State Farm ArenaPotential Game 6 venue remains uncertainAgenciesTue 13 Oct 2026 13.50 EDTLast modified on Tue 13 Oct 2026 16.11 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThe WNBA has moved up Game 3 of the finals by a day so theAtlanta Dreamcan host theGolden State Valkyriesat State Farm Arena. The league has also moved up the tipoff time for Game 4 of the best-of-seven series.Game 3 will now take place on Wednesday 21 October. Game 4 will tip off at 1pm ET on Saturday 24 October, two and a half hours earlier than originally scheduled.‘I’m supposed to be here’: Angel Reese’s road from ridicule to the WNBA finalsRead moreThe Dream had hoped to play at State Farm Arena, the home of theAtlanta Hawks, which seats more than 17,000 fans, rather than their regular home, Gateway Center Arena, which holds only 3,500. The series begins on Saturday in California.“We are grateful for the efforts made by numerous stakeholders, including the Dream, the Valkyries, the Hawks, State Farm Arena, and NBC Sports and USA Sports,”WNBAcommissioner Cathy Engelbert said.“The change of venue dramatically expands the seating capacity and ensures that the Dream will be able to provide an extraordinary atmosphere for the first WNBA finals game to be played in theAtlantamarket since 2013. We are pleased that thousands more fans across the Southeast region will have the opportunity to experience the ultimate WNBA action – the WNBA finals – in person.”Quick GuideWNBA finals 2026ShowScheduleBest-of-seven series. All times Eastern.Sat 17 OctGame 1: Atlanta at Golden State, 3.30pm (NBC)Mon 19 OctGame 2: Atlanta at Golden State, 8pm (USA/CNBC)Wed 21 OctGame 3: Golden State at Atlanta, 8pm (USA/CNBC)Sat 24 OctGame 4: Golden State at Atlanta, 1pm (NBC)Mon 26 OctGame 5: Atlanta at Golden State, 8pm* (USA/CNBC)Thu 29 OctGame 6: Golden State at Atlanta, 8pm* (USA/CNBC)Sat 31 OctGame 7: Atlanta at Golden State, 8pm* (USA/CNBC)*-if necessaryHow to watchIn the US, the series will air on NBC, USA Network and CNBC, with all games streaming on Peacock. In the UK, it will be carried by Sky Sports. In Australia, fans can watch through WNBA League Pass, with selected coverage also available through ESPN.Was this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.There had been scheduling conflicts at State Farm Arena for both games, with a concert by singer Sombr on 22 October and the Hawks hosting their home opener on the night of 24 October.“We are thrilled that we will be able to accommodate the Dream as they host Games 3 and 4 of the WNBA finals at State Farm Arena,” said Andrew Saltzman, president of business enterprise and chief commercial officer of the Hawks and State Farm Arena.View image in fullscreenAtlanta Dream players Naz Hillmon, Angel Reese and Rhyne Howard celebrate after defeating the New York Liberty in Game 3 of their WNBA semi-final series at Barclays Center in New York on Friday.Photograph: Ishika Samant/Getty Images“Playing for a championship is special, and we want the Dream to feel the full support of the city during this amazing run.”skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Weekly for the 2026 WNBA seasonSign up toWNBA 30A limited run women’s basketball newsletter dedicated to the league’s historic 30th season.Enter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionWhile the Dream played most of their regular-season games at Gateway Center Arena, they moved six regular-season games and their three previous home playoff games to State Farm Arena. They will play all their home games there next seasonafter signing a multiyear dealearlier this month.The Dream, led by a core of Angel Reese, Rhyne Howard, Allisha Gray and Jordin Canada, are making their first finals appearance in 13 years aftersweeping the Mysticsin the first round andthe 2024 champion New York Libertyin the semi-finals.It remains unclear where Game 6 would be held if the series goes that far, with the Hawks scheduled to play another home game at State Farm Arena on 29 October.The Valkyries faced a scheduling conflict of their own for Game 2 on 19 October, whenDoja Cathad been scheduled to perform at Chase Center in San Francisco. That concert has been moved to 25 October.Explore more on these topicsWNBAAtlanta DreamAtlantaAngel ReeseAtlanta HawksDoja CatGolden State ValkyriesShareReuse this content

title: Josh Allen finally gets first OT victory of his career as Bills beat Rams in thriller | NFL | The Guardian
description: Josh Allen accounted for 331 total yards, and Tyler Bass made a 45-yard field goal in OT shortly after Greg Rousseau blocked the Rams’ own attempt
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Josh Allen accounted for 331 total yards, and Tyler Bass made a 45-yard field goal in OT shortly after Greg Rousseau blocked the Rams’ own attempt
Content: Tyler Bass celebrates his winning kick for the Bills.Photograph: Luke Hales/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenTyler Bass celebrates his winning kick for the Bills.Photograph: Luke Hales/Getty ImagesNFLJosh Allen finally gets first OT victory of his career as Bills beat Rams in thrillerBuffalo Bills 37–34 Los Angeles Rams (OT)Allen was 0-7 in overtime coming into gameQuarterback rushes for 121 yards on wild nightRams have field goal blocked in overtimeAgenciesTue 13 Oct 2026 00.05 EDTLast modified on Tue 13 Oct 2026 09.22 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleJosh Allen accounted for 331 total yards and two touchdowns, Tyler Bass made a 45-yard field goal with 1:55 left in overtime shortly afterGreg Rousseau blocked the Rams’ own attempt, and the Buffalo Bills outlasted Los Angeles for a 37-34 victory on Monday night.Allen passed for 210 yards and rushed for 121 more for the Bills (4-1), who rallied to win a frantic game befitting the teams with the NFL’s last two MVPs at quarterback. Allen won an overtime game for the first time in his career – he had previously been 0-7 – by besting Matthew Stafford, who passed for 383 yards and three touchdowns.The Deshaun Watson revival derailed, much to the joy of those with a functional memoryRead more“Guys kept chipping away, defense kept going out there making plays, special teams was big tonight,” Allen said after the game. “Don’t think we threw it very well, especially in the first half but our team kept fighting. We found a way to win, it’s the first OT [win] I’ve got, so it feels good being on this side.”Kyren Williams scored on a one-yard surge with four seconds left in regulation for Los Angeles. The Bills began overtime by driving deep into Rams territory before Aaron Donald recovered James Cook’s fumble, the second time the running back had fumbled on the night.Stafford drove the Rams to the Buffalo 30, but Harrison Mevis missed his second field goal attempt of the night when Rousseau got a piece of it.Allen then had scrambles of 19 and 13 yards to set up the kick by Bass, who ran away to celebrate before the officials signaled it good.Allow content provided by a third party?This article includes content hosted onembed.bsky.app. We ask for your permission before anything is loaded, as the provider may be using cookies and other technologies. To view this content,click 'Allow and continue'.Allow and continue“They got a really good defense and there was some opportunity there in the quarterback scramble game, just trying to extend some plays,” Allen said. “Got a lot of things to clean up but I’ll take being 1-0 on this two-game west coast trip.”Puka Nacua had a career-high 17 receptions for 138 yards and a score for the Rams (2-3), who are under .500 after five games for the fourth time in five seasons.Allen, however, said he had nothing but respect for his opponents, particularly their quarterback.“If he’s not the greatest thrower of a football of all time, I don’t know who is,” Allen said of Stafford.There was a brief flare of tempers after the game when Rams tackle Alaric Jacksonpunched Bills linebacker Bradley Chubb. The pair exchanged words before the incident, and neither player was wearing a helmet, although Chubb did not seem bothered afterwards.“It’s just emotions, you know what I mean? Emotional game. It was a close game,” Chubb told the California Post. “And, you know, they always catch the second guy. So, I let him swing. And then my teammates held me back, and I just chilled.”Explore more on these topicsNFLBuffalo BillsLos Angeles RamsUS sportsnewsShareReuse this content

title: Maresca says he would describe Manchester City as ‘cheats’ if he were a United fan | Manchester City | The Guardian
description: Enzo Maresca has admitted he would describe Manchester City as ‘cheats’ if he were a Manchester United or Arsenal fan
Author: Jamie Jackson
Headline: Enzo Maresca has admitted he would describe Manchester City as ‘cheats’ if he were a Manchester United or Arsenal fan
