Content: Enzo Maresca’s Manchester City side host Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League on Wednesday.Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The GuardianView image in fullscreenEnzo Maresca’s Manchester City side host Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League on Wednesday.Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The GuardianManchester CityMaresca says he would describe Manchester City as ‘cheats’ if he were a United fanManager claims City fans suffering more than playersLuis Enrique says club should keep all titles wonJamie JacksonTue 13 Oct 2026 09.31 EDTLast modified on Tue 13 Oct 2026 14.05 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleEnzo Maresca has admitted he would describe Manchester City as “cheats” if he were a Manchester United or Arsenal fan. The manager’s ­comments came as he suggested it had been harder for City’s supporters todeal with the scandalsurrounding the club than it had been for him or the players.Maresca guided City to an ­impressive 3-0 win at Liverpoolon Sunday in their first game since the club were found guilty of more than 100 charges related to breaches of the Premier League’s financial rules. He was asked whether the performance was down to the team being brought closer together bythe guilty verdict.Manchester City v PSG is a reminder of the path not taken in sanctions battlesRead more“It probably has been more tough for our fans than for the players or for me as it’s more complicated,” he said, “because if I am an Arsenal fan or a United fan and you are a City fan, I can tell you: ‘Hey, my friend, you cheat’ – or this kind of thing. But we were happy at the end of the game and inside the changing room. We were very happy celebrating the three points because we know how difficult it is at Anfield.”City, who have appealed against the independent commission’s ­ruling and continue to protest their innocence, have drawn criticism for theexuberant manner of Sunday’s celebration. Maresca defended the revelry but is conscious of the need to focus on Wednesday’s visit of Paris Saint-Germain in their second Champions League game of the season, following their 2-0 victory at Porto.“We won 0-3 at Anfield,” Maresca said. “Even if it was 0-1 it would be exactly the same. We are here today to win tomorrow’s game and we work every day to win games. It’s the only thing that we can think; we can be focused. The rest is just things from outside that we need to deal with but we were so happy inside the pitch and you cannot imagine inside the changing room.View image in fullscreenEnzo Maresca (right) talks with Enzo Fernández during a training session on the eve of the clash against PSG.Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The Guardian“I promise you that I stress a lot about the gameplan and how we can train every day but I don’t stress about things I don’t [control]. The message to the players will be the same. We know how serious the situation is but at the same time it’s not something that we can do [anything about].”Rúben Dias, City’s captain, echoed his manager. “When you build yourself as a player, you build yourself against any noise,” the defender said. “Personally, and I feel like I speak for the whole group, we’re very calm. We trust the club, and we’re very focused on enjoying football. People don’t love us winning and we love to win.”Pep Guardiola isexpected to be at the Etihad Stadiumon Wednesday in a show of support for City’s owners. “In case he’s coming, it’s a nice feeling,” Maresca said of his predecessor. “Especially for him, because this has been his house for 10 years. It’s exciting for everyone.”skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionLuis Enrique, PSG’s head coach, said City should keep all the ­trophies won from 2009-18, the timeframe of the guilty charges. “The first time that you hear [about the verdict], is it is a surprise,” he said. “But we need to respect the process and wait for the final decision. The authorities are responsible for making these decisions. But speaking only about football, they deserved those trophies. I love their football. Beyond that, we have to wait for the judges’ decision.”Luis Enrique played with ­Guardiola at Barcelona. The 56-year-old was asked what he would say to his ­former teammate. “Nothing ­serious,” he said. “The trophies you win on the pitch remain on the pitch. They deserved to win that and I hope they can avoid the sanction. But we have to wait. The things I will say to Pep I will do in private.”City claimed three Premier League titles, one FA Cup, and three League Cups in the nine-year span.Explore more on these topicsManchester CityEnzo MarescaFootball politicsChampions LeaguenewsShareReuse this content

title: Christian Pulisic is no longer a focal point for the US or Milan – and that’s OK | Christian Pulisic | The Guardian
description: The winger is 28, and younger teammates are rising into the high-pressure spots he has usually occupied
Author: Jeff Rueter
Headline: The winger is 28, and younger teammates are rising into the high-pressure spots he has usually occupied
Content: Christian Pulisic missed the US’s recent international friendlies.Photograph: Marco Bertorello/AFP/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenChristian Pulisic missed the US’s recent international friendlies.Photograph: Marco Bertorello/AFP/Getty ImagesChristian PulisicChristian Pulisic is no longer a focal point for the US or Milan – and that’s OKThe winger is 28, and younger teammates are rising into the high-pressure spots he has usually occupiedJeff RueterTue 13 Oct 2026 05.00 EDTLast modified on Tue 13 Oct 2026 09.54 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleUsually, the second weekend of October seesChristian Pulisicflanked by compatriots as the Star-Spangled Banner plays. Last year, he was involved in US friendlies against Ecuador and Australia. But this year, with Fifa having folded the October window into September, Pulisic didn’t have the chance. On Sunday, his pre-match music was O Generosa, the Serie A anthem, which he observed with a soft smile.Mark Twain’s first visit to Italy left him describing the country as “a vast museum of magnificence and misery”, and it’s a fitting summary of Pulisic’s three-plus years withMilan. The magnificence: 43 goals and 25 assists in 138 appearances. The misery: just one trophy since he arrived in July 2023, a 2025 Supercoppa Italia held in Saudi Arabia.For years, Pulisic’s club career was a source of chronic frustration in between the reprieve of international duty. Now, after Mauricio Pochettino opened the team’s next era by selecting 13 top prospects (but not Pulisic, recently recovered from injury), his international standing is in a shakier state than ever, a decade after he debuted.With no Pulisic and good results, have the USMNT moved on from their savior complex? | Leander SchaerlaeckensRead moreIn a continuation of a frustratingly familiar theme, Pulisic’s fourth season with Milan hasn’t started smoothly. The lower-leg microfracture he suffered against Belgium at the World Cup this summer has kept him off Ruben Amorim’s teamsheet, with just two league starts. He opened Sunday’s visit to Sassuolo as the right half-space winger beneath Gonçalo Ramos.Pulisic still commands quite a lot of attention. Mid-table Sassuolo were more willing to let the ball find Diego Moreira than Pulisic, with the American’s touches garnering additional defensive bodies. As opponents converged whenever he entered the final third, he often cycled possession to fellow US international Yunus Musah, trailing behind on the right side of midfield.Pulisic dropped into the defensive half often in search of creating numerical advantages, part of a relatively free-roaming deployment. He led Milan players with 5.3km (3.2 miles) covered in the first half, although his industry failed to create much. He was a key part of the buildup to Milan’s only goal of the day, playing the pass before Luka Modric’s assist and offering the Croat a helpful decoy run.By the 77th minute, Pulisic’s sole shot had been blocked and his only created chance was stifled by the goalkeeper. Pulisic has a goal contribution in just four of his last 22 appearances in Serie A.Having turned 28 last month, Pulisic is in the next, veteran phase of his career. Teams expect an attacker nearing 30 to be prolific. A player who is steady if unspectacular at this point can fall down the depth chart if a younger, more dynamic alternative presents themself.View image in fullscreenChristian Pulisic celebrates after scoring a goal.Photograph: Tiziano Ballabio/NurPhoto/Getty ImagesWith a quarter-hour left against Sassuolo, Amorim opted for one: Pulisic off, Alpha Cissè in.Since arriving from Hellas Verona this summer, Cissè has been a bright spot for Milan. The 19-year-old was lauded by Amorim early in the season, starting as Pulisic recovered from his World Cup injury. In just 242 league minutes, Cissè has scored twice; Pulisic, now up to 190 minutes under Amorim, has one goal.“I love Cissè. I love Cissè,”crooned the coachin late August.That’s not to say that everything is against Pulisic. This week,Gazzetta dello Sport reportedhe is one of three key players the club hopes to renew early in the Amorim era. He has history to fall back on, having led Milan with 17 goals in all competitions two seasons ago.“I can only say that I am very happy at Milan right now and for the near future as well,” Pulisic said at a San Siro meet-and-greet during the window, flanked by a wall of shirts bearing his name. “So, yeah, I’m not thinking about the contract renewal but I am very happy here. I want to stay at Milan.”skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Twice weeklySign up toSoccer DeskJonathan Wilson and Guardian journalists bring expert analysis and reporting on the biggest stories in soccer.Enter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionCissè’s rising presence mirrors Pulisic’s new reality with his national team. Pochettino ushered in the next generation as Pulisic remained in Italy, giving debuts to several teenage attackers who are hungry to work into the fold. Cavan Sullivan validated the hype with anaudacious account-openeragainst Mexico, while others – such as wingers Mathis Albert andnew Crystal Palace signing Zavier Gozo– began what they hope will be long careers representing the US.Zavier Gozo: ‘You have to be uncomfortable to get to the highest levels’Read morePulisic has struggled on international duty under Pochettino. He’s scored just once since the start of 2025, in a tune-up friendly against Senegal.His mostly poor performances at the World Cuphardly reinforced his bona fides to the Argentinian, who declined to directly address Pulisic’s situation during the recent international window.It’s far too soon to write Pulisic off. He covers considerable ground. His more decisive touches can generate threats, though too often he appears caught in two minds about his best course of action. After years of being cast by Milan and, especially, the US as an attacking focal point, he may be more dangerous as an auxiliary option with a lower touch volume.Internationally, his rising teammates could afford Pulisic a lower-pressure role. Sullivan has relished early acclamation of being the face of the program. Folarin Balogun weathered the pressure – well, the more normal kinds – of being the team’s chief goalscorer at the World Cup, bagging three goals in 316 minutes. With Pulisic absent, Pochettino used his usual spot at left-wing to shoehorn in both of his chief playmakers, Gio Reyna and Malik Tillman; given his past form at Milan, he could still slot in at right-wing while making Sullivan a useful alternative to all three from the bench.Pulisic’s entire careerhad been framedin the context of a home World Cup. Perhaps being freed from that years-long pressure can enable him to rediscover his best form, to Milan’s benefit as well as his national team’s.But with the World Cup gone and his performances leaving something to be desired, we’re left to wait and watch to see who Pulisic is, and will be, as a player.Explore more on these topicsChristian PulisicUSAMilanUS sportsfeaturesShareReuse this content

title: James and Russo lead rout of Greece as ruthless England set up Ukraine playoff | Women's World Cup 2027 qualifiers | The Guardian
description: Two goals from Lauren James and Alessia Russo helped England to a 5-0 win over Greece (8-1 on aggregate) that sets up a World Cup playoff against Ukraine
Author: Suzanne Wrack
Headline: Two goals from Lauren James and Alessia Russo helped England to a 5-0 win over Greece (8-1 on aggregate) that sets up a World Cup playoff against Ukraine
Content: Lauren James (left) is congratulated by fellow goalscorer Alessia Russo after netting her second and England’s fourth goal.Photograph: Nick Potts/PAView image in fullscreenLauren James (left) is congratulated by fellow goalscorer Alessia Russo after netting her second and England’s fourth goal.Photograph: Nick Potts/PAWomen's World Cup 2027 qualifiersJames and Russo lead rout of Greece as ruthless England set up Ukraine playoffPlayoff semi-final second leg: England 5-0 Greece (agg 8-1)Goalscorers: Russo 3 75, James 16 34, Stanway 30Suzanne Wrackat the King Power StadiumTue 13 Oct 2026 16.41 EDTLast modified on Tue 13 Oct 2026 18.45 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleA mercurial Lauren James scored two and provided an assist in a thrilling four-goal first 45 minutes against Greece, as England put themselves two games away from securing their place at the World Cup.James’s double was matched by Alessia Russo, who scored either side of the break, and her Arsenal ­teammate Georgia Stanway was also on the scoresheet, with the Lionesses setting up a playoff final against Ukraine in November and December. It was a clinical and slick statement from England, albeit against a team they should bypass with ease.Any Greek hopes of arriving in Leicester and launching a Trojan horse-style smash and grab, after a hugely impressive performance in their3-1 defeat by an ­unconvincing Lionessesteam in Crete, were quickly dashed.England v Greece: Women’s World Cup qualifying playoff, second leg – liveRead moreSarina Wiegman had said on the eve of the game that she wanted to see improvement in the final third. In the King Power Stadium, which had a club vibe to it before kick-off as dance remix after dance remix blared out, the Lionesses responded to their manager’s call, Russo producing the first goal from the first shot and first attack in the third minute.James was the architect, the ­Chelsea player driving forward and picking out the No 9, who shrugged clear of Eleni Markou’s challenge before firing a low shot in.View image in fullscreenAlessia Russo gets England up and running with a third-minute goal.Photograph: Andrew Boyers/Action Images/ReutersIt was Russo’s fourth goal in four games for club and country, with the Arsenal forward having gone five Women’s Super League games without a goal before this run, and it was a sign of things to come from a team keen to shake off criticism of their lack of ruthlessness.James was in majestic form, her injury worries behind her this season, and England fans were treated to a glimpse of what they missed at the Euros in Switzerland in 2025, when a less than half-fit James struggled and looked frustrated as her body failed to meet her demands on it.James has said that the best is yet to come from her and Wiegman agreed. “I think so,” said the manager. “She was really enjoying herself, scored some great goals, but also picked up some great positions. I thought she looked really fresh and played well.”On the Chelsea forward’s use more centrally, having previously been preferred in a wider role, Wiegman said: “As a winger or inverted winger she does similar things. She can play any position up front, right or left, because she’s right- and left-footed. When she plays on the outside she also gets the opportunity to come inside, and I think she can do both things then, and that’s when she comes to life.”James delivered England’s ­second and fourth in Leicester, her two first-half goals sandwiching ­Stanway’s header into the far corner from ­Lauren Hemp’s chipped cross.View image in fullscreenGeorgia Stanway heads in England’s third goal as they swiftly put the result beyond doubt.Photograph: Andrew Boyers/Action Images/ReutersFor her first, the 25-year-old ­cushioned Maya Le Tissier’s pass before sending a rising drive goalwards with her left foot. Her second was far simpler, the unmarked forward turning in Hemp’s ball from close range.Job well and truly done, James was withdrawn at half-time in favour of Beth Mead, Wiegman’s jewel safely nestled back in a velvet pouch after shining so brightly.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toMoving the GoalpostsNo topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionWiegman leapt on the opportunity presented by the 7-1 aggregate scoreline to rotate ­further at the hour mark, with Niamh Charles, Jess Park and Freya Godfrey given a chance to demonstrate why they should be on the plane to Brazil should England overcome Ukraine.Whether the changes took the sting out of the game or England just eased back on the intensity given the margin did not really matter because the home team remained in complete control of the ball. Their more than 50-place superiority in the Fifa world rankings was far more ­evident in Leicester than it had been in Heraklion.Russo was the beneficiary of ­England’s patience as the clock ticked down, collecting Keira Walsh’s angled pass before she raced clear, stepped around Styliani­Katergiannaki in the Greece goal and rolled the ball into the empty net.“I think today we played a lot better,” said Wiegman. “We totally dominated the game … As soon as we got in behind and we scored that goal that helped and I think after that we were really, really good in the final third.”Ultimately, despite the performance put on there isvery little to be learnedfrom a game against a team so far below England’s level. Any slip-up would only ever have been of England’s own making, as the poor defending for Greece’s goal in Crete demonstrated. However, perhaps that sluggishness could be ­attributed to a rustiness after a four-month break from international football.Ukraine are up next, the homeless team preparing to face the European champions after a 4-1 aggregate defeat of Slovakia.England met Ukraine in their World Cup qualifying group earlier in the year and secured a 9-1 margin across the two matches, so it would take the most almighty of collapses for the Lionesses to fail to book their place in Brazil now.Quick GuideRoundup: Scotland and Wales advance to playoff finalsShowMelissa Andreatta claims herScotlandside “stuck to our principles” in the 3-2 win overCzechiawhich booked a place in round two of the Women’s World Cup play-off against Sweden.Leading 2-0 from the first leg of the round one play-off but losing Caroline Weir to an injury in the warm-up at St Mirren’s Marbill Coaches Stadium, Scotland found themselves a goal down in the third minute when the Czechis full-back Denisa Vesela sent a shot from 30 yards soaring over a helpless Sandy MacIver. That lead lasted only two minutes before Lauren Davidson clipped in an equaliser from 12 yards but the visitors steeled themselves again and in the 32nd minute Klara Cahynova headed in a corner from Michaela Khyrova.However, Kathleen McGovern levelled early in the second half following a botched clearance by the Czechia defender Lucie Bendova and in the 72nd minute, when Barbora Votikova, the visiting goalkeeper, spilled a cross from the substitute Erin Cuthbert, Christy Grimshaw was on hand to lift the ball over the line and the home side ran out deserved winners.The Scots will take on Sweden, who beat Lithuania 10-0 on the night and 15-0 on aggregate, in a two-legged tie with the matches taking place between 26 November and 5 December, with Scotland at home first.Andreatta told BBC Scotland: “What it showed is what Scotland’s all about.“We stuck to our principles, ground out a result and that puts us in a good place for what’s ahead. I think these two games being so tough and testing us in all different ways, gives us the confidence to go again against Sweden."Walestook a step towards qualifying for the Women’s World Cup for the first time after a 3-0 win overAlbaniaat Parc y Scarlets. Rhian Wilkinson’s side, who won the reverse fixture 1-0 in Shkoder last week following Ezmiralda Franja’s own goal, also set a new national record after extending their unbeaten run to 10 matches.Any nerves on the night were eased when Mayzee Davies headed home in the 34th minute, while Elise Hughes and Hannah Cain struck after half-time to seal a comprehensive 4-0 aggregate triumph. Wales will next take on Norway in their playoff final in December for the right to head to Brazil next year. Norway sit 13th in the world rankings, 18 spots higher than Wales.Kess Elmore marked her firstNorthernIrelandstart with a goal but could not prevent them from falling to a 3-1 loss toPortugal, completing a 7-1 aggregate defeat in their playoff.TheRepublic ofIrelandputKazakhstanto the sword again, claiming a 12-0 aggregate win to move closer to qualifying. An 8-0 victory in last week’s first leg in Astana meant the Republic were all but home and hosed.Jessie Stapleton bagged the Republic’s final goal in the Kazakh capital and the Leicester defender opened the scoring just before half-time, while Katie McCabe struck just after the interval. The substitute Lucy Quinn and Denise O’Sullivan were also on target as the Republic cruised into the play-off final, where they will take on Poland across two legs in December.Press AssociationWas this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.Explore more on these topicsWomen's World Cup 2027 qualifiersEngland women's football teamWomen's footballmatch reportsShareReuse this content

title: Timber’s touch of class and supersub Saka secure Arsenal win against Lille | Champions League | The Guardian
description: Eberechi Eze was also on target as Arsenal scored three goals in seven second-half minutes in a 3-0 win against Lille in the Champions League
Author: Ed Aarons
Headline: Eberechi Eze was also on target as Arsenal scored three goals in seven second-half minutes in a 3-0 win against Lille in the Champions League
Content: Jurriën Timber clips Arsenal into a second-half lead against Lille.Photograph: Ed Sykes/Allstar Picture Library/SportsphotoView image in fullscreenJurriën Timber clips Arsenal into a second-half lead against Lille.Photograph: Ed Sykes/Allstar Picture Library/SportsphotoChampions LeagueTimber’s touch of class and supersub Saka secure Arsenal win against LilleEd Aaronsat the Emirates StadiumTue 13 Oct 2026 17.02 EDTLast modified on Tue 13 Oct 2026 18.29 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleTwelve wins in a row and counting. On a night when Arsenal remembered Ken Friar – the club’s life president who was instrumental in their move from Highbury to the Emirates in 2006 – it was fitting that Mikel Arteta’s side should rack up yet anotherChampions Leaguemilestone at their home that has become a fortress.Such has Arsenal’s dominance been here in recent seasons that when Bukayo Saka slotted home their third against a dogged Lille side, it was the 36th goal they have scored at the Emirates in the league or group stage since returning to Europe’s top table under Arteta three years ago. In those 12 wins, they have remarkably conceded only three times.Barrios strikes after 53 seconds as Atlético pile misery on 10-man Manchester UnitedRead moreArsenal have also now racked up 14 successive league-stage victories in this competition – three short of Bayern Munich’s record – even if Arteta’s side were made to work for this one and had to wait until the 64th minute to find the breakthrough. That came from the unlikely source of Jurriën Timber after Arsenal’s second-string attack – and Viktor Gyökeres in particular – had looked laboured. But while Arteta may be concerned that it needed the introduction of Saka from the bench along with Martin Ødegaard and Kai Havertz to put this game to bed as Eberechi Eze added a second before Saka rounded off the scoring with a third in the space of seven minutes, they never looked in any danger of losing their proud record as Olivier Giroud received a standing ovation on his return to north London.“I’m sure he is very happy to see how the boys played. But not only that, because I know how proud he felt about what we built,” said Arteta of Friar. “It’s a really sad day for everyone who loves football. The legacy that Ken is going to leave for this club is going to be for ever.”Arsenal had earlier paid tribute to Friar, who worked his way up from the box office to club secretary before becoming managing director in the 1980s, when his death at the age of 92 was confirmed. The players wore black armbands as a mark of respect. Friar would have been especially proud of their formidable record here under Arteta in this competition that stretches back to the 2023-24 season, when they returned to the tournament after an absence of six years. It is little wonder that Arteta was so reluctant for redevelopment plans to go ahead given the disruption any temporary move away to Wembley or elsewhere would have caused.Despite the absence of Piero Hincapié and Martín Zubimendi after they were both injured during the warm-down after the victory over Leeds on Saturday, the Arsenal manager was still able to make five changes. Lille’s manager, Davide Ancelotti, who worked under his father, Carlo, at Everton and Real Madrid among others before being appointed during the summer in only his second senior role, resisted the temptation to start with 40-year-old Giroud against his former club.View image in fullscreenBukayo Saka slots home Arsenal’s third goal from close range.Photograph: Matthew Childs/Action Images/ReutersRestored to his favoured right flank after excelling on the left against Leeds, it had not been saying much that Noni Madueke had once again been Arsenal’s most dangerous outlet in a first half in which they struggled to create much against a deep-lying defence.Bruno Guimarães and then Mikel Merino spurned decent chances, while Ayase Ueda had the ball in David Raya’s net after Nabil Bentaleb’s shot deflected off Timber and hit Hákon Haraldsson on the way through, with the video assistant referee confirming the Japan striker was marginally offside.But Arsenal lacked creativity without Ødegaard and Gyökeres showing plenty of hustle and bustle yet making little real impact.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionIt summed Arsenal’s first half up when he could not get out of the way after Eze forced Berke Ozer into his first proper save and was promptly flagged offside. Ozer then had to scramble the ball away from the feet of the Sweden striker after spilling a shot from Guimarães on the stroke of half-time.The referee, Felix Zwayer, waved away appeals at the start of the second half when Guimarães went down in the area under pressure from Alexsandro but the Arsenal midfielder seemed to be looking for the contact. A wayward effort that almost made it into the upper tier from Madueke was the signal for Arteta to summon Ødegaard, Saka and Havertz to get ready.Before they had time to be introduced, Arsenal finally found the breakthrough when Madueke picked out Timber to apply a deft finish with his right foot after a brilliant first touch. Saka made an immediate impact by setting up Eze to dispatch the second with his left foot – possibly with the help of a deflection – less than three minutes later, before adding a third after combining with Havertz and Ødegaard. Lille must have wondered what had hit them.As well as the chance to pay their respects to Giroud, the Arsenal fans were treated to a late cameo from the dazzling Max Dowman to round off another very satisfying evening that has become the norm.Explore more on these topicsChampions LeagueArsenalLillematch reportsShareReuse this content

title: Championship roundup: racist chanting mars Swansea’s win at Millwall | Championship | The Guardian
description: Swansea scored a last-minute winner to stay top of the Championship but game at Millwall held up by racist chanting
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Swansea scored a last-minute winner to stay top of the Championship but game at Millwall held up by racist chanting
Content: Ronald (left) celebrates scoring a late winner for Swansea in their game at Millwall, which was suspended for almost seven minutes due to racist chanting.Photograph: Ben Whitley/PAView image in fullscreenRonald (left) celebrates scoring a late winner for Swansea in their game at Millwall, which was suspended for almost seven minutes due to racist chanting.Photograph: Ben Whitley/PAChampionshipChampionship roundup: racist chanting mars Swansea’s win at MillwallRonald’s last-minute winner keeps Welsh side on topMiddlesbrough edge Stoke in thriller; Watford gloomPress AssociationTue 13 Oct 2026 17.52 EDTLast modified on Tue 13 Oct 2026 18.57 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleSubstitute Ronald scored a last-minute winner to keepSwanseatop of theChampionshipafter their match atMillwallwas held up for almost seven minutes due to a complaint about racist chanting at the Den.The referee, Edward Duckworth, halted the match in the 65th minute and walked to the dugouts to speak with Lions manager, Alex Neil, Swans counterpart Vítor Matos and fourth official Ruebyn Ricardo.Joy for Eckert as 10-man Southampton edge out Portsmouth in feisty derbyRead moreA security guard was also on the scene, with the referee seeming to point to an area in the stands behind the Swansea dugout. When play eventually resumed it was announced in the stadium that there had been a report of racist chanting, adding that police were working to identify any offenders using CCTV.But the unsavoury incident could not take the gloss off a dramatic last-gasp 1-0 victory for the table-toppers.The Brazilian defender Neto Borges bagged a dramatic injury-time winner after earlier scoring an own goal as high-flyersMiddlesbroughsecured a thrilling 3-2 victory over battlingStoke.The 30-year-old netted his first league goal for 18 months as Boro stay second in the table after stretching their current unbeaten run to five games.Callum Brittain had fired the visitors ahead three minutes into the second half before Junior Tchamadeu’s shot deflected in off Borges for an unfortunate own goal soon afterwards.The England Under-21 hitman Will Lankshear restored the visitors’ lead with his eighth league goal in 10 games after Stoke keeper Viktor Johansson inexplicably spilled Brighton loanee Amario Cozier-Duberry’s left-foot strike from the edge of the area. It took the striker to the top of the Championship scoring charts.Substitute Robert Bozenik looked to have earned the home side a point, slotting home after Boro skipper Luke Ayling’s poor clearance with five minutes left, but Borges scored from close range in the first of four minutes of stoppage time.View image in fullscreenNeto Borges fires in Middlesbrough’s winner.Photograph: Nigel French/PAWatford’s woeful season took another turn for the worse as they conceded four first-half goals in a 5-1 defeat atCardiffto drop into the relegation zone.Rising Republic of Ireland star Jack Moylan scored twice in the first half, winning and converting an 11th-minute penalty and then picking his spot to beat Federico Ravaglia in a one-on one in the 35th.Hornets skipper Mattie Pollock had brought down Moylan for the penalty and then headed into his own net from a corner in the 41st minute before Ollie Tanner added the fourth in the fifth minute of first-half added time.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionBirminghamunderlined their growing promotion credentials with a commanding 4-0 victory over 10-manPrestonat St Andrew’s. Two goals from August Priske and one each for Liam Millar and Demarai Gray gave Chris Davies’ men a third win in four games – and their first at home. Preston, who played most of the second half with 10 men, remain rooted to the bottom of the table.Ivan Mesik scored a dramatic last-gasp leveller forCharltonto clinch a 2-2 draw atBurnley, extending the hosts’ 360-day wait for a home league win. Largie Ramazani’s 57th-minute goal putBurnleyinto a 2-1 lead at Turf Moor, but substitute Mesik denied equalised with virtually the last kick of an absorbing contest.West Bromstaged a dramatic late revival to beatWrexham2-1 at Stok Cae Ras. Kieffer Moore’s stunning second-half strike gaveWrexhamhope that they could claim back-to-back home wins for the first time since February. But West Brom scored twice in five minutes through Isaac Price and Aune Heggebo to stop the rot after derby defeats to Wolves and Birmingham.Wolvessuffered their first home league defeat of the season asBoltonwon 3-1 at Molineux. Atsuki Ito gave Steven Schumacher’s visitors a deserved 28th-minute lead and although Jean-Ricner Bellegarde equalised five minutes after the break, substitute Sam Dalby and Josh Sheehan struck in the last 20 minutes to seal victory.A magnificent goalkeeping display from Balazs Toth inspiredBlackburnto a 1-0 victory overBristol Cityat Ashton Gate. Toth was simply unbeatable on the night, making a string of outstanding saves, particularly in the first half. Oladapo Afolayan rifled home the only goal in the 38th minute.PosTeamPGDPts1Swansea109232Middlesbrough106213Birmingham106174West Brom102175West Ham911166Stoke101167Blackburn102158QPR93149Wolverhampton921410Millwall1001411Bristol City10-21412Charlton10-31413Southampton9101314Bolton10-31315Sheff Utd911216Wrexham10-41117Lincoln City9-41118Cardiff1011019Norwich9-2920Portsmouth8-2821Burnley10-4822Watford10-11823Derby9-7624Preston North End10-124Explore more on these topicsChampionshipMillwallSwansea CityMiddlesbroughStoke CityWatfordCardiff CityShareReuse this content

title: Football regulator chair insists he will resign if politically pressured over Manchester City | Football politics | The Guardian
description: David Kogan said he would resign if he faced political pressure on how to respond to Manchester City being found guilty of breaching Premier League financial rules
Author: Paul MacInnes
Headline: David Kogan said he would resign if he faced political pressure on how to respond to Manchester City being found guilty of breaching Premier League financial rules
Content: Concern had been raised that the proximity of Manchester City’s ownership to the Abu Dhabi state could trigger a political intervention by the UK government.Photograph: Loannis Alexopoulos/Anadolu/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenConcern had been raised that the proximity of Manchester City’s ownership to the Abu Dhabi state could trigger a political intervention by the UK government.Photograph: Loannis Alexopoulos/Anadolu/Getty ImagesFootball politicsFootball regulator chair insists he will resign if politically pressured over Manchester CityKogan says he has faced ‘absolutely no political pressure’Regulator wants deal on redistribution through leaguesPaul MacInnesTue 13 Oct 2026 12.00 EDTLast modified on Tue 13 Oct 2026 13.41 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThe chair of the Independent ­Football Regulator (IFR), David Kogan, has said he will resign if he faces any political pressure on how to respond to Manchester Citybeing found guiltyof breaching Premier League financial rules over a nine-year period, insisting “my independence is absolute”.Kogan could remove City’s Abu Dhabi United Group (ADUG) should the damning verdict of an independent commission be upheld at the end of an ongoing appeal process. ­Concern had been raised, however, that the proximity of City’s ­ownership to Abu Dhabi’s rulers could trigger a political intervention by the UK ­government and an immediate test of the new regulator’s powers.Burnham’s meeting with City’s al-Mubarak and other contact with club disclosedRead moreThose concerns have been rebuffed by Kogan. “Our independence is absolute and my independence personally is absolute,” he said. “I [have] made it very clear … any form of political interference on the way we operate is going to result in my resigning from this role, and I stand by that completely. And, just to be crystal clear, we’ve come under absolutely no political pressure whatsoever on this or any other topic.”Kogan was speaking on Tuesday at the launch of the long-awaited State of the Game report, a document that lays out the financial challenges facing the English football pyramid. The City case has cast a huge shadow as the regulator prepares to introduce a new licensing regime for clubs later this season. “We have powers within the legislation that allow us to review not only owners and directors and senior executives, but also whether those owners are fit and proper ­people to run clubs going forward,” said Kogan, describing the process by which the regulator might intervene.“That process is reliant on us ­having very detailed knowledge and information, which requires a ­certain amount of investigation. Then we would take judgments based on the legal advice that we then receive.”Should a club owner ultimately be found to have failed a “fitness” test related to “integrity, honesty and financial soundness”, the regulator could force the club to be sold. “We deal with issues of this type much more frequently than you might realise because we are constantly looking at clubs,” Kogan said, stating if any decision by the regulator became the subject of legal action then clubs would be asked to foot the bill through a funding levy.View image in fullscreenDavid Kogan reiterated that the regulator had powers to determine whether owners such as Manchester City’s were ‘fit and proper’.Photograph: Ben Whitley/PAThe acceleration of revenues among the Premier League’s biggest clubs is one of the key findings in the State of the Game report. The highest earning top-flight club currently earns 605 times the revenue of the lowest earning National League club. At the same time, spending has increased at all levels of the game, with 94% of the 116 clubs under the regulator’s regime posting a financial loss in 2025-26. In one particularly eye-catching statistic, the report found 11 Football League clubs recorded costs that exceeded their income even once player wages had been stripped out.Kogan argued that a number of external factors that fall outside the regulator’s purview are affecting the game, including the expansion of the club calendar, the regulation of ­players’ agents and the recent rise in interest rates. However, he argued that one key measure – the agreement of a redistribution deal between the Premier League and EFL – could unlock change immediately.While Kogan accepts the Premier League’s argument regarding the need for parachute payments due to “colossal” drops in revenue caused by relegation, he believes they have had a “distortive effect that’s grown over the years”. Kogan said that if a deal was done that reduced parachute payments but increased the amount going to all clubs then “that will go some way towards looking at the ­distorted effect”. Once that money was distributed, he said, “you’re going to see a softening effect going through down the 116 clubs”.View image in fullscreenManchester City’s owner, Sheikh Mansour, and chair, Khaldoon al-Mubarak, are under scrutiny.Photograph: Martin Rickett/PAThe Premier League welcomed the publication of the report, arguing: “It recognises what English football has built – the world’s most popular league, the leading second tier, and a pyramid of unmatched depth.”The league argued that a recent offer of financial redistribution to the EFL – understood to amount to £320m per season – “meets the ­objectives the IFR has set out in its report” and said it “remains ­committed to concluding a long-term partnership with the EFL that is fair, generous and ­balances the interests of all clubs”.The EFL said the report’s findings “reinforce the EFL’s longstanding position that English football generates sufficient revenue to sustain both a successful Premier League and a thriving pyramid” and it remained “committed to working constructively with the Premier League and the regulator to secure a financial settlement in the interests of the whole game”.Meanwhile, the secretary of state for digital, culture, media and sport, Lisa Nandy, said the stark figures covered in the report had “blown the doors off the game”. She urged football authorities to “consider these findings for the good of the game, for the fans, and for the communities of which they are so often the bedrock”.Explore more on these topicsFootball politicsFinancesManchester CitynewsShareReuse this content

title: Champions League roundup: Tresoldi treble stuns Inter in Club Brugge win | Champions League | The Guardian
description: Club Brugge beat Inter 4-3 at San Siro thanks to Nicolò Tresoldi’s triple while Michael Olise was sent off in Bayern Munich’s 3-3 draw at Viking Stavanger
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Club Brugge beat Inter 4-3 at San Siro thanks to Nicolò Tresoldi’s triple while Michael Olise was sent off in Bayern Munich’s 3-3 draw at Viking Stavanger
Content: Club Brugge's Nicolò Tresoldi celebrates with the match ball after his hat-trick at San Siro helped earn his team a famous 4-3 win against Inter.Photograph: Daniele Mascolo/ReutersView image in fullscreenClub Brugge's Nicolò Tresoldi celebrates with the match ball after his hat-trick at San Siro helped earn his team a famous 4-3 win against Inter.Photograph: Daniele Mascolo/ReutersChampions LeagueChampions League roundup: Tresoldi treble stuns Inter in Club Brugge winInter 3-4 Club Brugge; Galatasaray 1-4 BarcelonaOlise sent off as Bayern held 3-3 at Viking StavangerAFP and ReutersTue 13 Oct 2026 18.07 EDTLast modified on Tue 13 Oct 2026 18.58 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleClub Bruggeand their young forward Nicolò Tresoldi shockedInter4-3 at San Siro in the Champions League’s result of the night. Tresoldi, a 22-year-old Italian-born Germany Under-21s forward, scored the first three goals for the Belgian side.A Hakan Calhanoglu foul on Carlos Forbs resulted in a penalty which Tresoldi slotted in just before the half hour. Tresoldi picked up his second after capitalising on a blunder by the Inter keeper Josep Martínez and reacted faster than the Inter defence for the third with a quarter of an hour to go.Lautaro Martínez had given his team a lifeline just before the break after a move initiated by Marcus Thuram, followed by a Federico Dimarco back-heel assist. The Argentinian then gave the San Siro crowd hope again in the 81st minute by narrowing the score to 3-2, but Romeo Vermant once again exposed Inter’s defensive fragility by adding a fourth goal in the 87th minute. Ange-Yoan Bonny pulled a goal back for the home side in the third minute of stoppage time.Barrios strikes after 53 seconds as Atlético pile misery on 10-man Manchester UnitedRead moreHaving lost 2-1 to Real Madrid at the Bernabéu in their opener, Inter remain on zero points and will be under immense pressure to win next week at home against Shakhtar Donetsk. Brugge, who lost at home to Aston Villa on matchday one, will next host the French club Lens.Bayern Munichwere held 3-3 atViking, with the Norwegian champions equalising late through Herman Haugen after Michael Olise was sent off. Bayern trailed 2-0 at half-time thanks to goals from Gianni Stensness and Peter Christiansen. Harry Kane seemed to have dragged Bayern to victory as he scored twice and set up another for a 3-2 lead, but Olise picked up two yellow cards in the space of a minute.View image in fullscreenViking’s Herman Haugen (second right) celebrates after scoring his side’s third goal against Bayern Munich.Photograph: Lise Åserud/NTB/APViking made the most of their advantage with Haugen scoring in the final minute to snatch a shock draw for the Norwegian champions against the German giants. Olise’s red means he will miss next week’s blockbuster clash with Arsenal in Munich.Barcelonaand Lamine Yamal rediscovered their sparkle after a rocky first-half spell in the cauldron of Istanbul’s Ali Sami Yen stadium to win 4-1 againstGalatasaray.The Turkish club took the lead after 27 minutes. After Anthony Gordon went tumbling in the penalty area, the hosts launched a rapid counterattack through Rafael Leão on the left. He pulled the ball back to the edge of the area to the Russian Aleksey Batrakov, whose drive deflected off João Cancelo and into the net.That ignited a spell of furious home pressure which culminated with Victor Osimhen rising to head a corner past Joan García. Baris Yilmaz toed the ball over the line but was ruled offside.Barcelonareasserted control, and when Lamine Yamal went down on the edge of the box, the ball broke to Davinson Sánchez, who gave it away immediately. It fell to Dani Olmo, who threaded a pass for Cancelo to score.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionView image in fullscreenLamine Yamal was on sparkling form as Barcelona won 4-1 in Istanbul.Photograph: EPAAt the start of the second half, Lamine Yamal took over. After setting up Gordon, who spurned the chance, he helped put Barça ahead in the 50th minute, placing a gentle curled cross on the forehead of Fermin López, who nodded home.Three minutes later, Lamine Yamal beat Eren Elmali three times, and in three different ways, in a tiny space before rolling a pass to Gordon in front of goal. This time the England attacker made no mistake. After 65 minutes, Lamine Yamal cut in from his wing and fired a pass to Gabriel Jesus. The former Arsenal man, on as a substitute, could not control the ball but it deflected to Karim Adeyemi who drilled the ball home.Villarrealrecovered to beatNapoli3-1 at home with goals from Georges Mikautadze, Santiago Mouriño and Tani Oluwaseyi. Brajan Gruda’s 75th-minute strike gaveRB Leipziga 1-0 win overPSV Eindhovenafter Maarten Vandevoordt had saved Ivan Perisic’s early penalty with a boot.The Azerbaijani outsidersSabahclaimed a historic first win in the league phase, beatingSlavia Prague2-0. Second-half goals from Kaheem Parris and Joy-Lance Mickels secured the historic win in Baku for a club that was founded only nine years ago.In the other early kick-off,Sportingalso sealed a 2-0 win, prevailing atLensthanks to goals in either half from Luis Suárez and Issa Doumbia.Explore more on these topicsChampions LeagueClub BruggeInternazionaleBayern MunichViking FKBarcelonaGalatasaraynewsShareReuse this content

title: Iraola has ‘100% trust’ in Wirtz and Barcola but tells others to step up | Liverpool | The Guardian
description: Andoni Iraola said: ‘We need other players to give us those numbers,’ as he prepared for Liverpool’s Champions League game at Lask without Alexander Isak and Cody Gakpo
Author: Andy Hunter
Headline: Andoni Iraola said: ‘We need other players to give us those numbers,’ as he prepared for Liverpool’s Champions League game at Lask without Alexander Isak and Cody Gakpo
Content: Florian Wirtz has Andoni Iraola’s support despite only one assist this season.Photograph: Adam Vaughan/EPAView image in fullscreenFlorian Wirtz has Andoni Iraola’s support despite only one assist this season.Photograph: Adam Vaughan/EPALiverpoolIraola has ‘100% trust’ in Wirtz and Barcola but tells others to step up‘We need other players to give us those numbers’Liverpool face Lask in Austria without Isak and GakpoAndy Hunterin LinzTue 13 Oct 2026 13.20 EDTLast modified on Tue 13 Oct 2026 13.49 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleAndoni Iraola has said he trusts Liverpool’s big-money signings Florian Wirtz and Bradley Barcola “100%” but needs players to step up in the absence of his three leading goalscorers.Liverpool will again be without Alexander Isak, Cody Gakpo and Dominik Szoboszlai when visiting the Austrian side Lask in theChampions Leagueon Wednesday. Iraola said he did not know when any of the trio, all of whom are carrying minor injuries sustained on international duty, would be available.Cherki cracker caps Manchester City win at Liverpool in face of Anfield tauntsRead moreTheir absence heightened the responsibility on Wirtz and Barcola against Manchester City on Sunday but both struggled as Liverpool suffered their first defeat under Iraola. Barcola is yet to produce a goal or an assist in six appearancessince his £123m arrivalfrom Paris Saint-Germain, or even win possession in the final third, while Wirtz has one assist this season and continues to underwhelm in a Liverpool shirt.“Cody, Alex and Dom are our top scorers this season and now we don’t have them. We need other players to give us those numbers,” said Iraola. “We trust the players we have now to play in those positions. With Bradley and Flo, they have had good games and bad games this season like everyone else. We know their level and we know they will give us good performances.“The other day, if [Lewis] Koumas scores the goal that he connects with really well, then it is one assist for Bradley Barcola. His performance would be exactly the same but we will all say: ‘Oh, he played really well with an assist.’ Sometimes we focus only on the numbers. With Bradley, the other day he had good situations and we did not finish them. Bradley and Flo are players that I trust 100%.”View image in fullscreenBradley Barcola (left) has not won possession in the final third this season.Photograph: Jon Super/APThe Liverpool head coach confirmed he was likely to make changes in Linz, with several players knocks against City.Iraola insisted he was happy with the team’s spirit, attitude and work rate in Sunday’s defeat, “including from the offensive players”, but not with the collective response to Ryan Gravenberch’s harsh dismissal. “A lot of what happened after we went down to 10 men was because we conceded straight away,” Iraola said. “We were making adjustments and then you go 1-0 down and it’s different, because then you have to go [for it] and you get caught in-between.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotion“The goal we conceded straight away hurt us. If we had made the adjustments earlier and been more compact at 0-0, it becomes a lot easier. But once you concede it’s not enough to just be compact. You need to go a little bit more and then spaces open.”Virgil van Dijk is in line to captain Liverpool for a 200th time in all competitions on Wednesdaytonight.Explore more on these topicsLiverpoolChampions LeaguenewsShareReuse this content

title: Patrice Motsepe’s Caf presidency under pressure after Afcon U-turn as Eto’o waits in wings | Football politics | The Guardian
description: Patrice Motsepe’s leadership of the Confederation of African Football (Caf) is under growing pressure, with officials from across the continent warning they have lost trust in the president
Author: Romain Molina
Headline: Patrice Motsepe’s leadership of the Confederation of African Football (Caf) is under growing pressure, with officials from across the continent warning they have lost trust in the president
Content: Patrice Motsepe’s potential rivals for the Caf presidency are trying to gain Gianni Infantino’s approval should Motsepe step down early.Photograph: Themba Hadebe/APView image in fullscreenPatrice Motsepe’s potential rivals for the Caf presidency are trying to gain Gianni Infantino’s approval should Motsepe step down early.Photograph: Themba Hadebe/APFootball politicsPatrice Motsepe’s Caf presidency under pressure after Afcon U-turn as Eto’o waits in wingsRivals lining up to position as potential replacementsAfcon tournament expected to return to biennial cycleEd AaronsandRomain MolinaTue 13 Oct 2026 12.12 EDTLast modified on Tue 13 Oct 2026 15.16 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GooglePatrice Motsepe’s leadership of the Confederation of African Football (Caf) is under growing pressure, with officials from across the continent warning they have lost trust in the president and rivals including Samuel Eto’o positioning themselves potentially to replace him.A return to a biennial Africa Cup of Nations (Afcon) cycle is expected to be confirmed at Caf’s executive committee meeting in Abidjan next month after Motsepe surprisingly announced the U-turn last week – 10 months after the decision was taken tohold it every four years. That move is said to have wide support within Africa, but several sources have said there has been a weakening of trust in Caf’s leadership, with some questioning Motsepe’s management.Most national association presidents are said to have been unaware Motsepe intended to announce the proposed change to Afcon’s frequency until the issue was raised at a strategic conference in Cape Verde last week. Motsepe confirmed he was not intending to stand for re-election for a third time when his term expires in 2029 and pledged Africa’s “unconditional support” for Gianni Infantino’s re-election as the Fifa president in March on the “unanimous” behalf of all 54 of Caf’s member associations.It is understood Infantino remains extremely popular in Africa even though there are 10 to 15 member associations who would consider voting against him, asrevealed in August. Motsepe’s potential rivals for the Caf presidency are believed to be attempting to gain Infantino’s approval should the South African billionaire be persuaded to step down early.View image in fullscreenFormer Barcelona forward Samuel Eto’o is the president of Cameroon’s federation and a member of Caf’s executive committee.Photograph: Steve Luciano/APThey include Eto’o, the former Barcelona and Inter striker, who is the president of Cameroon’s federation and a member of Caf’s executive committee, Ahmed Yahya of Mauritania, Côte d’Ivoire’s Yacine Idriss Diallo, and Souleiman Waberi, a Fifa council member from Djibouti who has been chargedwith embezzlement and money laundering. He has denied the allegations. Other candidates may emerge from southern Africa.Sources indicate that Infantino could hold the key to whether Motsepe continues. The other option would be to challenge Motsepe through Caf’s statutory mechanisms, which say an extraordinary general assembly can be convened after a written request from at least two-thirds of the members of the executive committee.Infantino is thought to have fallen out with Motsepe after Motsepe allowed the Somali referee Omar Artan, who was denied entry to the United States for the 2026 World Cup, to take charge of Uefa’s Super Cup final in August amid growing tensions with European football’s governing body. However, sources have indicated their relationship has improved in recent weeks as Infantino has sought to solidify his support in Africa.Motsepe promised annual distributions of about $700,000 (£528,000) from Caf to each association at the conference in Cape Verde – an increase of $500,000 – and is understood to have increased payments to executive committee members for attending meetings from $150 to $350, and to have introduced for them an annual bonus payment of about $8,000.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionThat is despite growing concerns over Caf’s finances, with a broadcast deal signed with IMG due to expire after the 2027 Afcon. Asreported by the Guardianin February, there are major doubts about whether that tournament will go ahead owing to questions over the readiness of Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda to host in June and July. Some sources are predicting that tournament could be pushed back to Christmas and the new year, which would cause major disruption to the European club season.Caf is believed to have broadcast offers for future tournaments from IMG and an unnamed firm, although it is not known how the package will be structured and whether the proposed return to a two-year cycle could affect its commercial value. A Caf spokesperson said the process remained ongoing and that no rights had been awarded.Explore more on these topicsFootball politicsnewsShareReuse this content

title: ‘I expect more’: Lisandro Martínez hits out at Manchester United hierarchy | Manchester United | The Guardian
description: The Argentinian said the Champions League defeat to Atlético was ‘a reflection of the mirror of how our club is’, adding: ‘I expect more from our technical director’
Author: Sid Lowe
Headline: The Argentinian said the Champions League defeat to Atlético was ‘a reflection of the mirror of how our club is’, adding: ‘I expect more from our technical director’
Content: Lisandro Martínez came out with some fierce criticism of Manchester United after defeat in Madrid.Photograph: PSNEWZ/SIPA/ShutterstockView image in fullscreenLisandro Martínez came out with some fierce criticism of Manchester United after defeat in Madrid.Photograph: PSNEWZ/SIPA/ShutterstockManchester United‘I expect more’: Lisandro Martínez hits out at Manchester United hierarchyDefeat to Atlético Madrid ‘reflects how our club is’Argentinian says club has not invested enough in playersSid Loweat the Riyadh Air MetropolitanoTue 13 Oct 2026 18.48 EDTLast modified on Tue 13 Oct 2026 19.08 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleLisandro Martínez has hit out at theManchester Unitedhierarchy, blaming the lack of investment as their dismal start to the season continued. Goals from Pablo Barrios and Ademola Lookman pushed United to a 2-0 defeat at Atlético Madrid, and the Argentina defender described that as a “mirror” of the way the club are. “Tonight it is easy to say the coach, easy to say the players but also we have to see other areas,” he said, pointing upwards.Asked for his appraisal of the night, Martínez said: “Really poor, really poor. I have to control myself a lot but sometimes is a reflection of the mirror of how is our club at the moment.Barrios strikes after 53 seconds as Atlético pile misery on 10-man Manchester UnitedRead moreIt is annoying, disappointing coming here and I am not seeing my team trying to get an amazing result here.“I expect more [investment], 100%. I expect more from our technical director [Jason Wilcox]. I have to be honest, as players we have to do more but it is also important when you make a strong squad to be ready for this kind of night. Last season we did everything, we created the base to create an amazing team.”United won 12 of 17 games under Michael Carrick last season but during the summer they made only three major signings – Carlos Baleba, Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans – plus the back-up goalkeeper Karl Darlow on a free transfer from Leeds, and have won only twice in all competitions so far this term. They have suffered the worst start to a league campaign in 40 years.Asked if the manager had been backed sufficiently, Martínez replied: “I don’t think so. He does his best. Every season is different. You can’t stay with what you did last season. The teams knows how you play, they know every detail, if you don’t change next season [it] is a big problem.“You can’t keep changing, changing, changing the manager. What about other areas?” Martínez added, looking up. “I can’t say more.”View image in fullscreenLisandro Martínez said afterwards: ‘You can’t keep changing the manager. What about other areas?’Photograph: PSNEWZ/SIPA/ShutterstockWhen Martínez’s words were put to Carrick, he said: “I haven’t seen the interview. I have half-heard about it. I think it’s a little bit the emotions of the game [talking]. I have to find out a bit more about it to be honest to decide what and if anything is going to be done. I can’t comment further.”United’s manager also insisted that his side had “four almost one vs ones” and that he did not understand Leny Yoro’s red card on a night when they could have gone back to Manchester with a different result. “It is easy to look and think there is something deeply wrong, I understand that, but the players have been great,” he said. “There’s willing, and [they are] disappointed that they haven’t come out of here with something. We think we could have, should have.”Explore more on these topicsManchester UnitedAtlético MadridChampions LeaguenewsShareReuse this content
